chunks.title: Tokenised stocks, priced two ways
chunks.text: The Gully Labs tracker checks every tokenised stock on Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain and Solana against its fair price, live. These docs cover how it works, the public API it is built on, the widget that puts it on your own page, and the products built around it. Docs for Gully Labs: the stock token tracker on Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain and Solana, its public API, the widget and API keys, plus Gully Pay, the Holder Map, Gully AI, the Telegram bot, swaps and status.

chunks.title: Tokenised stocks, priced two ways
chunks.text: For each stock token the tracker reads two prices: the fair price, from the Chainlink feed for that stock, read on chain; and the onchain price, what the token trades at in its deepest pool. The difference, as a percentage of fair, is the gap. A token trading above its fair price is at a premium; below it, at a discount. The live page is at gullylabs.xyz/tracker. Everything it shows comes from the same public API these docs describe. It covers three chains: Robinhood Chain (Robinhood’s stock tokens), BNB Chain (Binance bStocks) and Solana (Backed’s xStocks). How Solana differs is on the Solana page.

chunks.title: Tokenised stocks, priced two ways
chunks.text: Fair prices are Chainlink feeds read on chain with latestRoundData(); on Solana, where a share has no Chainlink feed, the issuer’s own xStocks quote, and every row names its source. Onchain prices are read from each token’s deepest pool on chain; DexScreener and GeckoTerminal only find the pool. Nothing is estimated or typed in: a price that cannot be read is reported as unreadable, never as zero. The methodology gives the exact rules. The tracker reports what two public sources say. It is not investment advice, and a gap is not a promise that anyone can trade it away.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: How each number is read, how the gap is computed, and the rules that keep a small pool or a closed market from making a headline. How the Gully Labs tracker reads a stock token's fair price from Chainlink and its onchain price from the deepest pool, and the rules that decide when a gap is flagged.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: For every token in the tracker’s feed table, on every chain it covers, two numbers are read live on each refresh: Fair: the Chainlink feed for that stock, read on chain. Onchain: the token’s price in its deepest pool, read straight from that pool’s contract. Both are in US dollars per token. Each is either a number or unreadable; an unreadable price is never replaced with zero or with an older figure.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: Every feed is read with latestRoundData() in one batched call per chain. A round whose answer is zero or negative, or whose update time is zero, counts as unreadable. The answer is scaled by the feed’s decimals. Robinhood Chain The feeds price the token itself (feedPrices: "tokenized-instrument"), so fair is the feed’s answer. BNB Chain The feeds price the underlying share (feedPrices: "underlying-share"). One raw bStock token is a number of shares given by the token’s own uiMultiplier() (ERC-8056, where 1e18 means 1.0). The multiplier is read on chain on every refresh, because the issuer changes it at a split. If the multiplier cannot be read, or reads as zero, the fair price is unreadable for that token. The multiplier used is returned in each row as multiplier.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: Once an hour the tracker asks DexScreener (GeckoTerminal if DexScreener refuses) for every pool of every token, 30 tokens per request. For each token it keeps the pools with a positive price and picks one: pools quoted against a native coin or a dollar stablecoin come first (WETH, ETH, WBNB, BNB, USDC, USDG, USDT, USD1, FDUSD), then the deepest by liquidity. Between those reads, every refresh prices the chosen pool from the chain itself: slot0() on a v3 pool, StateView.getSlot0 on a Uniswap v4 pool. The pool’s ratio is turned into dollars with $1 for a dollar stablecoin, Chainlink’s ETH/USD or BNB/USD feed for the native coin, and this cycle’s fair price where the quote is itself a stock token. The chain’s poolSource says on chain when this is the source. The row’s pool object names the pool used, its liquidity and 24-hour volume, and totals across every pool found for the token. Liquidity and volume come from the hourly read, because the chain does not publish them in a usable form.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: Every row carries a status, decided in this order: feed-unreadable (fair is null): The Chainlink feed (or, on BNB Chain, the multiplier) could not be read. pool-unreadable (pool read failed): DexScreener could not be read for this chain. no-pool (onchain is null): No pool with a usable price was found. unverified (onchain ≥ 5× or ≤ 1/5 of fair; or |gap| ≥ 15% unless the pool holds $1,000,000+ and was read on chain this cycle): The figure is implausible for a tokenised stock: far more often a bad print (a misread venue, an old API reading, a decimals slip) than a price. gapPct is withheld (null), the figure stays in rawGapPct, and untrustedReason says why. Never flagged, ranked, alerted on or recorded in the history. thin (liquidity < $10,000): The chosen pool is too small to trust. Shown, never flagged. in-line (|gap| < 1%): Within the noise. Robinhood Chain feeds only move on a 0.5% deviation. drifting (1% ≤ |gap| < 2%): Moving away from fair, not yet flagged. premium (gap ≥ 2%): Flagged: trading above fair. discount (gap ≤ −2%): Flagged: trading below fair. The thresholds are returned with every response in rules (minLiquidityUsd, inLinePct, flagPct, implausiblePct, trustLiquidityUsd, unitsRatio), so a client never has to hard-code them. The rules applied live: every trusted row’s gap right now, with the in-line band and the flag lines drawn from the same response’s rules. Hover a bar for its status. Trust and provenance

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: live: every trusted row’s gap right now, with the in-line band and the flag lines drawn from the same response’s rules. Hover a bar for its status. Trust and provenance Every row says whether the tracker stands behind its gap. trusted is true only for premium, discount, drifting and in-line rows whose pool read is fresh; otherwise untrustedReason gives the reason in a sentence (a thin pool, an implausible figure, an unreadable source, or a pool read served from the last good one while sources back off). Top movers and gap alerts only ever use trusted rows; the five-minute history skips every row without a gap (an unverified row included) and every stale pool read. onchainSource says where this cycle’s onchain price came from: chain when the pool contract was read directly, api when it is the price API’s reading for a venue that cannot be re-read on chain. onchainAt is when that price was read, so an API reading shows its own age.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: Stock feeds follow market hours. Each chain reports whether its session is open now: Robinhood Chain, 24/5: Chainlink’s US equities 24/5 session, Sunday 20:00 to Friday 20:00, New York time. BNB Chain, NYSE hours: 09:30 to 16:00 New York time, Monday to Friday. Outside its session a feed holds its last value, so the gap is measured against the last session’s close, not presented as a live mispricing. Market holidays are not modelled: on a holiday the session reads as open and the feed’s update time, returned as feedUpdatedAt, shows how old the fair price is.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: The tracker reads its sources at most once every two minutes. Every visitor and every API caller share that one read. If the chain cannot be read and neither API answers, that chain backs off (one minute, doubling, at most 30 minutes) and keeps serving its last good pool read, marked poolsStale: true with its time in poolsAsOf, and poolStale: true on each row. A pool read older than six hours is dropped rather than shown. Fair prices stay live throughout. Every five minutes one snapshot per token is recorded, and kept for seven days. Rows without a gap, or with a stale pool read, are not recorded. The history endpoint serves them.

chunks.title: Tracker methodology
chunks.text: The onchain price is one pool’s price as DexScreener reports it, not a volume-weighted average across venues. Liquidity figures are DexScreener’s, in US dollars. Only tokens in the tracker’s verified feed tables are covered; a stock token without a Chainlink feed on its chain does not appear. A gap may not be tradable: pool depth, fees, slippage and issuer rules all stand between a gap and a profit. The tracker reports what Chainlink and the pools say, with the rules above. It is not investment advice and makes no promise about any token.

chunks.text: Base URL (https://gullylabs.xyz): Every endpoint lives under /api, except /healthz and the Score badge. Methods (GET, OPTIONS): The data endpoints are read-only; anything else answers 405. The few POST routes (checkout, Gully AI, review requests, Solana) are listed with their section. Format (JSON): UTF-8. Times are ISO 8601 in UTC, except history points (Unix seconds) and gap-index points (Unix milliseconds). CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *): On /api/tracker*, /api/holders/*, /api/score*, /api/status, /api/plans, /api/alerts/channels and the Security list and stats: call them from any browser origin. Not found (404 {"error":"not found"}): Any unknown /api/… path answers JSON, never the HTML page. Prices are US dollars per token. Any price may be null, meaning it could not be read; it is never replaced with zero. Live, from your browser: the response time of /api/tracker, measured every 10 seconds while this tab is open, and the rows it returns by status.

chunks.text: The whole tracker: every chain, the rules, the sources and one row per token. Top level generatedAt (string (ISO)): When this answer was built. chains (Chain[]): One entry per chain, below. rules (object): The thresholds in force: minLiquidityUsd (pools below are “thin”), inLinePct (gaps below are “in line”), flagPct (gaps at or above are flagged), implausiblePct (a gap this wide needs a deep pool read on chain to be believed), trustLiquidityUsd (how deep that pool must be) and unitsRatio (an onchain price this many times fair, or this fraction of it, is a units error). sources (object): fair and onchain describe the two price sources; tables names the feed table used per chain. rows (Row[]): One per token. See Rows. chains[] key (string): Chain key used everywhere else: robinhood or bsc. id (number): EVM chain id (4663, 56). name (string): Display name. sessionOpen (boolean): Whether the chain’s feed session is open now. See sessions. sessionName (string): 24/5 or NYSE hours. fairMethod (string): How fair is derived on this chain, in words. poolsAsOf (string | null): Time of the pool read in use. poolsStale (boolean): True when the pool read is the last good one, served while every price source for that chain is backing off. poolSource (string | null): Where pool prices came from this cycle: on chain, DexScreener or GeckoTerminal.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: chain (string): Chain key. ticker (string): Stock ticker, e.g. NVDA. name (string): Company name. token (string): Token contract address. feed (string): Chainlink feed address. fair (number | null): Fair price in USD per token. feedPrices (string): tokenized-instrument (the feed prices the token) or underlying-share (it prices the share). multiplier (number | null): Shares per token from uiMultiplier() on BNB Chain; 1 on Robinhood Chain; null when the feed could not be read. feedUpdatedAt (string | null): When the feed last updated. feedError (string | null): Why the feed could not be read, if it could not. onchain (number | null): Price in the chosen pool, USD per token. gapPct (number | null): (onchain − fair) / fair × 100. Null unless both prices were read, and null on an unverified row (the figure is withheld; see rawGapPct). rawGapPct (number | null): The same gap before the plausibility check. Equal to gapPct on every row except an unverified one, where it keeps the figure that was withheld. Never chart, rank or alert on it. status (string): One of premium, discount, drifting, in-line, thin, unverified, no-pool, pool-unreadable, feed-unreadable. Rules in the methodology. trusted (boolean): Whether the tracker stands behind this row’s gap: true only for premium, discount, drifting and in-line rows whose pool read is fresh (not poolStale). Top movers and gap alerts use trusted rows only.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: One token’s gap history: a snapshot every five minutes. Seven days are open to everyone; paid plans keep more (see Plans & alerts). chain (string): Chain key, default robinhood. 2 to 12 lowercase letters. ticker (string, required): 1 to 8 letters or dots; case does not matter. days (integer, optional): Window in days, from 1 up to what your plan includes. Without it you get the last seven days, as before. Over your plan’s limit answers 403; past seven days the answer adds days and is not cached publicly. The answer is { chain, ticker, points }, where each point is a tuple [unixSeconds, gapPct, onchain, fair], oldest first. A chain or ticker the tracker does not know returns an empty points array, not an error.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: Top movers: how each token’s gap to fair, and its onchain price, changed over the last hour or day, computed from the same five-minute snapshots as the history. For every token the latest snapshot is compared with the snapshot closest to one window earlier. Only tokens whose status is trusted right now (premium, discount, drifting or in-line) and that have both points are ranked; nothing is interpolated. window (string, optional): 24h (default) or 1h. limit (integer, optional): How many rows per ranking, 1 to 50, default 10. chain (string, optional): Rank one chain only, e.g. bsc. ticker (string, optional): With chain: also return that token’s own change in stock (null when it has none). Top level window (string): 1h or 24h. windowSeconds (number): 3600 or 86400. toleranceSeconds (number): How far the earlier snapshot may sit from exactly one window ago: 15 minutes for 1h, 2 hours for 24h. Further than that and the token is left out. asOf (string | null): The newest snapshot compared. Null when nothing could be compared. from, to (string | null): The comparison times: to is asOf, from one window earlier. Each row carries its own exact pair. eligible (number): Tokens with both points and a trusted status. left (object): Why the others are out: untrusted, noHistory, staleHistory (latest snapshot over 30 minutes old), tooShort. historyHours (number): How many hours the longest series covers.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: One number for the whole market over the last day: the average absolute gap of the widest series, in 30-minute buckets. The series are the eight with the largest absolute latest gap whose latest point is under an hour old. Same gate, CORS and rate limit as /api/tracker; no parameters. top (number): How many series are averaged (8). tokens (string[]): The series used, as chain:TICKER. bucketMinutes (number): 30. points ([ms, avgAbsGapPct][]): Oldest first, 24 hours. Time in Unix milliseconds; the average to 3 decimals. generatedAt (string (ISO)): When it was computed (at most once a minute).

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: A 0–100 score for a contract, from nine checks you can read one by one. No key, no tracker limit; CORS * on every answer. Chains: base, ethereum, bnb, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, avalanche (or the chain id). How it is worked out: Gully Score. GET /api/score (The public index: { scores[], chains[], methodology }. Each score: chainId, chainKey, address, name, symbol, score, grade, coverage, computedAt, change. Listed contracts only, best first.): public, max-age=60 GET /api/score/methodology ({ version, minCoverage, ttlHours, components[], rules[] }: each component’s id, label, weight, source and what.): public, max-age=300 GET /api/score/:chain/:address (One contract: score (null under 40% coverage), grade (Strong, Fair, Weak, Poor), coverage, components[] (each available, score, value, reason, evidence), history, changes, links (page, badge, explorer), stale.): public, max-age=60 GET /score/:chain/:address/badge.svg (An embeddable 232 × 48 badge from the stored score; it never computes one. Letters-only chain keys.): public, max-age=3600 A stored score younger than six hours is returned as is. Otherwise it is computed, at most six times a minute per address and four at once; when that limit is hit, or the chain cannot be read, the stored copy comes back with stale: true, or 429 / 502 when there is none. An unknown chain is 404, the zero address 400, an address with no code 404.

chunks.text: The live totals on the Gully Labs home page: volume, TVL and fees across our projects, each read from that project’s own public API (and DefiLlama where noted) and added up in USD. No parameters, no key; cached on the server for a minute. No CORS header: read it from a server, not a browser on another site. generatedAt (string (ISO)): When this answer was built. totals (object): volumeAllUsd, volume24hUsd, tvlUsd, fees24hUsd, feesAllUsd: each the sum over the venues that publish it, or null when none does. covers names the venues in each total; unread the venues that could not be read. daily ({ t, v }[]): Daily volume in USD summed across the venues read; t in Unix seconds. venues (Venue[]): One per project (cartel-family, deepcore, peddleswap, peddles, peddlequest): state: ok with its figures, daily, counts, notes and source (url, readAt), or state: error with error. No key; Cache-Control: public, max-age=30 and CORS *. off means the component is not configured on this server (Telegram without a bot token, say); unknown means it has not been checked yet. chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: These limits apply to /api/tracker* and /api/holders/*; the other routes have their own, listed in their sections. Anonymous requests are limited to 60 a minute per IP address. Requests that carry an API key in Authorization: Bearer <key> are counted against the key instead, at 600 a minute. Windows are fixed one-minute windows. An unknown or revoked key answers 401. Every response also states the limit in force, so a client can read it rather than hard-code it: X-RateLimit-Limit (success): Requests allowed per minute: 60 anonymous, 600 with a Free key, more on a paid plan. X-RateLimit-Remaining (success): Requests left in it. Retry-After (429): Seconds to wait before trying again. Need more? Get a free key, instantly. A key on a paid plan gets that plan’s higher limit; see Plans & alerts.

chunks.title: API reference
chunks.text: Errors are JSON with a single error string. 400 (history: chain or ticker malformed): Check the parameters. Body: {"error":"chain and ticker"}. 400 (movers: window, limit, chain or ticker malformed): Use window=1h or 24h, a limit from 1 to 50, and a ticker only with a chain. 404 (an unknown /api/ path): Body: {"error":"not found"}. Check the path. 405 (a method other than GET or OPTIONS): Use GET. 401 (unknown or revoked API key): Check the key, or request one at app.gullylabs.xyz. 403 (history: days beyond what your plan includes): Ask for fewer days, or move to a plan with more history. The body names your limit in historyDays. 429 (rate limit exceeded): Wait for Retry-After seconds, or use an API key. 502 (the tracker could not be built at all): Retry in a minute. A partial failure is not a 502: it shows as unreadable rows.

Anything else draws a ticker. data-chain (all | robinhood | bsc): Which chain’s stocks. Default all. On a badge it picks the chain when a ticker exists on both. data-ticker (e.g. NVDA): Badge only, required: the stock to show. data-theme (dark | light): Default dark. data-limit (number, 1 to 60): Ticker: how many stocks in the strip (default every stock). chunks.title: API keys
chunks.text: Keys are free and issued instantly at app.gullylabs.xyz. There is no form and no approval: Press Connect wallet and pick any browser wallet or Coinbase Wallet. Your wallet address is your account; there is no email or password. Sign the message your wallet shows. It is Sign-In with Ethereum (EIP-4361): a signature, not a transaction, so it costs nothing and moves nothing. It names app.gullylabs.xyz, expires after ten minutes and can be used once. Open API keys, press Create key and name it. The key works at once. Copy it then: it is shown in full only once, because we store only a hash of it. Smart-contract wallets (EIP-1271, including ones not deployed yet, ERC-6492) are accepted on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain and Robinhood Chain. A sign-in lasts 30 days on that browser.

chunks.title: API keys

Revoke stops a key for good. The dashboard shows requests per hour or day for each key, the error rate, and the last 50 requests with status and latency. Answers served from the edge cache never reach our servers and are not counted. A key issued through the earlier request form keeps working. Link it to your wallet from the API keys page to manage it there.

The quote shows the feed, its round and when it last updated. If the feed is more than two hours old, no quote is given in that coin. chunks.text: GET /api/tracker/history takes days, up to what your plan includes. Without it the answer is the last seven days, unchanged. chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: An alert watches one stock (chain and ticker) or every stock the tracker follows, for one condition: gap ({ type: "gap", pct, direction }): The gap between onchain and fair price is at least pct percent. direction picks the side: above a premium (gap ≥ +pct), below a discount (gap ≤ −pct), or both (the default, and what alerts made before directions read as). status ({ type: "status", status }): The tracker flags the stock premium, discount, or either. Alerts are checked on every tracker snapshot, every five minutes. Per stock, an alert fires when its condition becomes true and re-arms once it is false again. It does not repeat while the condition simply stays true. Each alert sends at most one delivery every 30 minutes. Stocks that trigger during that pause go out with the next delivery if their condition still holds. Only rows the tracker would itself flag count: a readable feed and pool, a pool deep enough to flag, a fresh pool read and an open feed session. Anything else neither fires nor re-arms. Each delivery is logged in the dashboard with its HTTP status (the last 50 per alert). Use Test to send an alert.test delivery with no events. When a plan lapses, the alerts beyond the Free allowance stay listed but are paused until you delete some or upgrade; the oldest ones keep running.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: A second kind of alert watches DeepCore, the launchpad and DEX in the Gully Labs family, for new token launches. It has no stock: it watches one DeepCore chain, or every chain when chainId is left empty. deepcore-launch ({ type: "deepcore-launch", chainId }): A token launches on DeepCore on that chain: 56 BNB Chain, 999 HyperEVM, 4663 Robinhood Chain or 8453 Base; null for any of them. DeepCore’s public API (GET /v1/launches) is read every 90 seconds. Each launch fires once, the first time it is seen; after a restart nothing already seen is sent again. Only launches made after the alert was created count (with an hour of slack for indexer lag), so a new alert does not replay the backlog. One delivery at most every 5 minutes per alert: launches seen in the meantime wait and go out together, up to the 20 most recent. A paused, muted or over-the-plan alert neither sends nor queues: launches it missed are not sent later. It counts against your plan’s alerts like a gap alert, and delivers the same way: webhook, Telegram or both, signed the same way (see below). When DeepCore cannot be read, nothing fires and nothing is invented; the next good read catches up on launches it has not seen.

It reads the same 90-second cache as the alerts, says when the list is older because DeepCore could not be read, and names any chain DeepCore itself could not read. Launch information is not advice.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: We POST JSON with these headers: Content-Type: application/json, X-Gully-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-Gully-Signature (sha256= and the hex HMAC). Answer with any 2xx within 5 seconds; we do not follow redirects and do not retry, and the status is shown in your delivery log.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: The signature is HMAC-SHA256 with the alert’s secret over `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`. The secret (whsec_…) is shown once when you create the alert; New secret replaces it. Compare in constant time and refuse old timestamps. Webhook URLs must be https:// on a public address. The host is resolved before every delivery and private, loopback, link-local and other reserved addresses are refused. See API keys for keeping secrets out of browser code; the same applies here.

chunks.title: Plans & alerts
chunks.text: An alert can message a Telegram chat as well as, or instead of, calling a webhook. In the Alerts tab of the dashboard press Connect Telegram: it opens the bot with a one-time code (ten minutes, single use) that links the chat to your wallet account, so there is no chat id to copy. Add to a group does the same for a group; only the person who linked a group can unlink it. Then tick Telegram on any alert. Each message names the stock and chain, the gap, the onchain and fair prices, the status and the pool liquidity, with a link to the stock page. Open NVDA opens the stock page; Mute 24h pauses that alert, on every channel, for 24 hours. Resume in the dashboard ends a mute early. Deliveries appear in the alert's log like webhook ones, with the result Telegram gave. In the chat, /alerts lists your alerts and /stop unlinks. Anyone can ask the bot /gap NVDA (or /gap NVDA bsc) and /top for the five widest trusted gaps. A figure the tracker could not read is said to be unreadable, never shown as zero. Which channels the server offers is public at GET /api/alerts/channels.

chunks.title: Badges
chunks.text: Small SVG badges you can put on a README, a docs page or a project site. One family: the Gully Labs mark, a label and a value. The Gully Labs badge family: Gully Score, Holder Map, Gully Security and Built by Gully Labs, in three sizes and two themes, with HTML and Markdown snippets to copy.

chunks.title: Badges
chunks.text: Every badge has the same three parts: the Gully Labs mark, the product in upper case, and a value in a second field. They are plain SVG images, open to any origin, so they work in a README, in an email or on any site. Add ?size=S|M|L (20, 28 or 36 px tall, M by default) and ?theme=dark|light (dark by default). The Gully Score, Holder Map and Gully Security badges link back to their page; they are cached and never start a computation, a map build or a scan.

chunks.title: Badges
chunks.text: These are live badges, served by /badges/example/<kind>.svg with fixed example values. The tones: green for a healthy value, gold for a middle one, a solid gold field for a warning, grey when there is nothing to rate.

chunks.title: Badges
chunks.text: Replace 0x… or sec_… with the contract, token or report. The Holder Map takes a chain key and an address or ticker, like the map’s own links. A Gully Security badge exists only for a published report, see Gully Security.

chunks.title: Badges
chunks.text: Nothing is drawn from a font on your side. The letters are outlined paths of the brand kit’s own typefaces (Barlow Condensed Bold for the label, JetBrains Mono for the value), the mark is the kit’s mascot bust, the colours are the kit tokens, and every edge sits on a whole pixel, so the badge is crisp at 1x and 2x. The width follows the text exactly. Gully Score explains what its number means.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: Every wallet account is a workspace. Invite teammates by wallet or by link, give each a role, and see who changed what. Share one Gully Labs developer account with a team: workspaces, roles and what each may change, invites by wallet or by link, the activity log and CSV exports of usage and payments.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: When a wallet first signs in to the app dashboard, it gets its own workspace and is its owner. Everything in the portal belongs to the workspace: API keys, gap and DeepCore launch alerts, the linked Telegram chat, Gully Analytics, the plan and its payments. Members share all of it; nothing is copied per person. The workspace is named after its owner (0x1234…abcd’s workspace) until an admin or the owner renames it. A workspace holds at most 25 people, the owner included, and 20 open invites at a time. Membership is checked on every request. A member who is removed is moved back to their own workspace on their next request. If the owner’s wallet is blocked, the workspace is unavailable to every member.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: Every member can see everything in the workspace. A role decides what they may change: owner (everything): The wallet that owns the workspace. Cannot be removed or demoted, and is the only one who can add, change or remove admins. admin (keys, alerts, Telegram, Gully Analytics, billing, company details, the team): Invites and manages developers, billing members and viewers, and renames the workspace. developer (keys, alerts, Telegram, Gully Analytics): Creates, renames, rotates and revokes keys; manages alerts and analytics websites; can open Gully Analytics in one click (see single sign-on). Cannot pay or manage the team. billing (billing, company details): Buys and renews plans (tracker API and Gully Analytics) and keeps the invoice details current. viewer (nothing): Read-only: keys (prefixes only), usage, alerts, billing and the activity log. Your own profile, your sign-in sessions, switching workspace, leaving one and accepting an invite are open to every role. A request beyond your role answers 403 with {"code":"forbidden-role"}.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: Owners and admins invite from the Team tab, in two ways: By wallet. Enter the teammate’s address. The invite waits for that wallet: they sign in to the portal and accept it there. Nobody else can use it. By link. The portal makes a link (https://app.gullylabs.xyz/#invite=…) that anyone who signs in with a wallet can accept, once. The link is shown once; only a hash of it is kept, so it cannot be shown again. Send it privately. Every invite carries the role it grants and expires after 7 days. Accepted, revoked and expired invites stop working at once. Open invites can be revoked from the Team tab. Only the owner can invite, or revoke the invite of, an admin. Opening a link shows the workspace name, the role and who invited you before you accept. Unknown links and repeated attempts are rate limited per address. Owners and admins change a member’s role or remove them from the Team tab. Removing someone moves their sessions back to their own workspace, which is untouched.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: If you belong to more than one workspace, the portal’s workspace switcher lists yours first, then the others by name. The choice is kept for that sign-in session only, so two browsers can work in two workspaces. Members can leave a workspace from the Team tab; the owner cannot leave their own.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: The Activity tab lists who did what in the workspace, newest first, 50 at a time. It records: Keys: key.created, key.renamed, key.rotated, key.revoked, key.linked. Alerts and Telegram: alert.created, alert.updated, alert.tested, alert.deleted, telegram.linked, telegram.unlinked. Billing and analytics: billing.quote, billing.paid, analytics.trial, analytics.site_added, analytics.site_removed, analytics.password_reset, analytics.quote, analytics.plan. Team and account: team.invited, team.invite_revoked, team.joined, team.role_changed, team.removed, team.left, workspace.renamed, company.updated, profile.updated, sessions.revoked. Usage: usage.threshold, by system, when the workspace’s busiest key passes 80% or 100% of the plan’s per-minute limit (at most once a day per threshold). The owner can also have it sent to Telegram from their profile. Only successful changes are logged, and never a secret. A workspace keeps its newest 1,000 events and nothing older than 180 days. Where usage.threshold fires on each plan, and how many keys a workspace may hold, read live from GET /api/plans: Reading it from code Page backwards by passing the previous page’s nextCursor as ?cursor=. A cursor that has aged out answers 400: start again from the first page.

chunks.title: Teams & workspaces
chunks.text: Two downloads from the portal, for whatever workspace is active. Any member, viewers included, can download them. usage.csv (one per time bucket and key): Requests made with the workspace’s keys: hourly buckets for 24h and 7d, daily (UTC) for 30d. client_err is 4xx other than 429, limited is 429, server_err is 5xx. payments.csv (one per payment, oldest first): Every payment for the workspace’s plans (tracker API and Gully Analytics), with the asset, chain, transaction hash and an explorer link. Every text cell that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading ', so a spreadsheet shows it as text instead of running it as a formula. Cells with commas, quotes or line breaks are quoted. Files are UTF-8 with CRLF line ends.

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: Who really holds a token: the biggest wallets as bubbles, the ones that trade with each other in gold, and a plain check of every DeepCore launch. Any token on Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain, Base, HyperEVM and Solana can be mapped. How the Holder Map works: data sources per chain, clusters and hidden links, the launch health score part by part, live mode, alerts, the API and the honesty rules.

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: The Holder Map covers any ERC-20 token on Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain, Base and HyperEVM and any SPL token on Solana, plus DeepCore launches and the stock tokens the tracker follows. Paste an address at gullylabs.xyz/holders: it is first checked to be a token (an ERC-20 that answers decimals and total supply, or a Solana mint), and with no chain given every supported chain is checked at once (a token on several chains gives a picker). Launch checks and the health score are for DeepCore launches and launchpads we know; a plain token gets holders, clusters and concentration. Every bubble is a wallet, sized by its share of the total supply (or of the listed holders when the supply could not be read; the map says which). Grey bubbles are not people: trading pools, liquidity and token locks, burn addresses, the token’s own contract, DeepCore and Gully Labs contracts, and exchanges. They are never put in a cluster and never counted in the “top 10 wallets” figure. The summary line says how much the top 10 wallets hold and how much the largest connected cluster holds, across how many wallets. A few plain sentences follow it. For stock tokens the map also shows what the top wallets hold at the real share price, and whether they sit on a premium or a discount to it.

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: The map reads each token from the cheapest source that is complete, in this order: our own index of the chain’s Transfer logs on an archive node (every transfer, so balances are exact), then Blockscout, then Moralis (the biggest holders). A token with a very long history (over 40,000 transfers for tokens nobody listed, or too many chain reads) is not rebuilt in full: it gets a “top holders only” map, labelled as such with the reason, or, when no holder source is available on that chain, a plain “unavailable”. A chain without any source says “holder data is not available on this chain yet”. It never shows an empty or made-up map. Which chains map any token today, and how (full history or top holders), is shown on the Holder Map page and in GET /api/holders/sources. To keep the service fair, new maps of tokens nobody listed are limited per visitor (5 a minute) and across all visitors (30 a minute), address checks too (8 a minute per visitor); maps already built are free for everyone. DeepCore launches (BNB Chain, HyperEVM, Robinhood Chain, Base) (DeepCore’s own log index: every transfer since the launch, so balances are exact): Every transfer between mapped wallets since the launch

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: everyone. DeepCore launches (BNB Chain, HyperEVM, Robinhood Chain, Base) (DeepCore’s own log index: every transfer since the launch, so balances are exact): Every transfer between mapped wallets since the launch Any ERC-20 and stock tokens (Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain, Base, HyperEVM) (Our own Transfer-log index on an archive node (exact balances); past its caps or without one: Blockscout, then Moralis (top holders, labelled)): Every transfer since the token was deployed; for top-holders maps, the latest transfers Any SPL token and stock tokens on Solana (Every token account of the mint where the RPC allows it, else the 20 largest token accounts, merged by owner (labelled)): Not read on Solana yet Labels come from DeepCore’s list of its own contracts, the launch’s lock, the Gully Pay fee proxies, the tracker’s pool and public name tags (exchanges among them) from Blockscout’s metadata service.

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: Two mapped wallets are linked when one sent the token to the other. Linked wallets form a cluster, drawn in kit gold (the largest) or pale gold. A cluster is often one person or team spread across many wallets, but not always: read it as a reason to look closer, not as proof. A hidden link joins two mapped wallets through an address that is not on the map (it passed tokens between them). It is drawn as a small hollow node with dashed lines; its tooltip names the address. For DeepCore launches the deployer’s funding of other wallets is a link too.

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: Every DeepCore launch gets a score from 0 to 100, made of parts you can read one by one: whether the launch liquidity is locked, bundled buying in the first block of trading, snipers in the first blocks, the deployer’s share now, how much the top 10 wallets hold, and the deployer’s record of earlier launches. Each part shows its weight, the points it earned, the figure behind it and a plain reason. Tap a part on the map to light up the wallets behind it. Live: the newest DeepCore launches and their score right now, from GET /api/holders/launches. A launch whose map is still being built says so instead of showing a score. The score, its parts, the bundled and deployer warnings and the liquidity check are never behind a plan. A part that could not be read is left out of the score and marked “not known”; it is never counted as good or bad. The card says how many parts were counted. The weights are the server’s: the API returns each part’s weight and points, so what the page shows is what was scored. The deployer’s record lists their other DeepCore launches with what happened to each (still trading, liquidity pulled, deployer sold, unknown). A deployer with many launches is marked “Serial launcher”. Wallets of the largest cluster that also hold other launches are listed under “Same wallets elsewhere”, with links to those maps.

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: On a launch’s map page, live mode reads new transfers every 15 seconds: each one flows as a particle from sender to receiver (addresses that are not on the map come in from the edge), bubbles resize to the new shares, and a LIVE pill shows when the map last updated. Under reduced motion the particles are still lines that fade. The replay slider rebuilds holdings at earlier moments from the token’s own transfers: press play (1× or 4×) to watch holdings concentrate or spread since the launch.

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: “Alert me” on a map opens the Alerts tab of the app with the token filled in. Pick what to watch (the largest cluster, the top 10, or the deployer’s share) and a threshold; deliveries go to Telegram and webhooks like every other alert, and count towards your plan’s alerts. See Plans & alerts.

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: GET /api/holders/:chain/:token answers the whole map as JSON;.csv gives the holder list and /card.png a share card. Requests count against the same keys and limits as the tracker. Field by field: API reference. To put a map on your own page, use the widget script with data-gully-widget="holders": see the widget guide.

chunks.title: Holder Map
chunks.text: Nothing is estimated or typed in: every figure is read from the sources above, with the time it was read. A value that could not be read is shown as such, never as zero. Labels name only what a source says an address is. The map is information, not advice. Clusters and scores are signals to look closer, not verdicts on a person.

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: Show who holds a token, and how the biggest wallets are connected, on your own pages. One script tag, a plain iframe, or the JSON behind it. No key needed to start. Put the Gully Labs Holder Map on a launchpad or any site: the one-tag embed, the framed page, the public JSON API, the share card, and how to get a launchpad listed.

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: Embed: one HTML element and the widget script. The map appears inside a responsive frame. API: GET /api/holders/:chain/:token returns the whole map as JSON, with CORS open to any origin, and /card.png returns a share card. Listing: a launchpad can be added to the registry so its launches are recognised. See Get your launchpad listed. What a map contains, where its data comes from and the honesty rules are on the Holder Map page.

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: data-gully-widget (holders): Selects the Holder Map (the same script also draws the tracker widgets). data-chain (robinhood | bsc | base | hyperevm | solana): Required. Anything else shows “Holder Map: set data-chain and data-token.” data-token (address, or a ticker): Required: 1 to 64 letters and digits. The token address, or a ticker the tracker follows (data-ticker is accepted as an alias). data-height (360 to 2000): Pixels. Default 760; a value outside the range falls back to the default. data-api (URL): Origin to frame. Default https://gullylabs.xyz; only for testing against another deployment. The script adds one lazy-loaded iframe, full width of its element, with rounded corners and a dark background. Size the element to size the map. The map reads its own data inside the frame. Your page makes no requests for it and the script sends no key. Trades and shares open gullylabs.xyz in a new tab. A “Powered by Gully Labs” credit always shows; a white-label embed is reserved for a plan and is not built yet. If your site sends a Content Security Policy, allow the script and the frame: script-src https://gullylabs.xyz; frame-src https://gullylabs.xyz;

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: The script only builds this iframe. If you prefer to write it yourself, the address is https://gullylabs.xyz/embed/holders/:chain/:token, and it may be framed from any origin: Use the same chain keys and token rules as above. The page has no site chrome, so it fits a panel on a token page; give the frame at least 360 px of height.

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: GET /api/holders/:chain/:token (The map as JSON.:token is an address (a Solana mint on solana) or a tracked stock ticker. CORS: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.): public, max-age=60 when ok GET /api/holders/:chain/:token.csv (The holder list as CSV. Needs a plan that includes it, otherwise 403.): private, no-store GET /api/holders/:chain/:token/card.png (A 1200 x 630 share card, free for everyone. Always an image: a branded “coming soon” or “not ready” card when there is no map.): public, max-age=300 (60 when not ready) :chain is a key (robinhood, bsc, base, hyperevm, solana) or the numeric chain id. An unknown chain is 404; a token that is neither an address nor a tracked ticker is 400. Anonymous calls are limited per IP address; an API key (Authorization: Bearer gl_live_…) raises the limit to its plan. See API keys and the API reference. A new map is built at most 12 times a minute per IP; cached maps are free. Call the API from your server for anything heavier than a page view. Maps are cached for at least five minutes, so polling faster returns the same answer.

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: Always check state first. HTTP status is 200 for ok and unavailable, 404 for not-found, 429 or 503 for busy and 502 for error. state ("ok" | "unavailable" | "not-found" | "busy" | "error"): Only ok carries the fields below. The others carry reason (plain words), chain, token.address and asOf; unavailable adds comingSoon. kind (string): What was mapped, for example stock or deepcore-launch. chain ({ key, id, name }): The chain. token ({ address, symbol, name, decimals, supply, url }): supply is null when the total supply is not known; url is the explorer page. asOf (ISO time): When the map was built. holders ({ count, shown, graph, sharesOf, partial }): sharesOf says whether percentages are of total supply or of the listed holders; count may be null. nodes[] (wallet): id, short, rank, balance, pct, label ({ kind, name } or null), contract, cluster (a cluster id or null), flags[] and url. On stock tokens also valueAtFairUsd, premiumUsd and boughtGapPct. links[] (edge): source, target, transfers, pct and kind (transfer, funding or via). clusters[] (group): id, wallets[], count, pct, hasDeployer. summary ({ top10Pct, largestCluster, line, plain[] }): The concentration in numbers and in plain sentences. forensics (object | null): Launch checks (deployer share, bundled and sniped buying, funding, liquidity lock). Null for tokens without a complete history. fair (object | null): Stock tokens: the fair-price overlay. timeline (frames | null): Replay frames; null on the free view. recentFlows[] (transfers): The latest large movements.

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: without a complete history. fair (object | null): Stock tokens: the fair-price overlay. timeline (frames | null): Replay frames; null on the free view. recentFlows[] (transfers): The latest large movements. legend[] ({ kind, text }): The label kinds present on this map. features, tier, locked[] (object, string, string[]): What this caller’s plan includes: features has replay, csv, alerts, holders, liveMinutes and gated. Amounts are in token units, shares are percentages (0 to 100, two decimals). A value that could not be read is null, never zero. Fields can be added over time; read the ones you need and ignore the rest. Related routes GET /api/holders/launches: the newest DeepCore launches on holder chains. GET /api/holders/top?limit=: the most scanned maps today. GET /api/holders/resolve?q=: find a token by name, ticker or address. GET /api/holders/sources: which chains have maps today.

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: /card.png is a ready-made preview of a map, drawn from the free view so everyone gets the same picture. Use it as an og:image or as a link badge that leads to the full map: The full map for any token lives at https://gullylabs.xyz/holders/:chain/:token.

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: A typed client and a React component are coming in @gullylabs/holders: createHoldersClient() with getMap() and cardUrl(), and a <HolderMap chain token height /> component that frames the embed above. It is not published yet; until then use the embed or the API directly. The tracker client and widget are in the SDK today.

chunks.title: Integrate the Holder Map
chunks.text: The Holder Map keeps a registry of launchpads. One declarative entry per launchpad is all it takes: its chains, and either a token endpoint on your API or the factory contract and the event it emits when a token is created. Peddles and PeddleSwap are the first two entries. What we need from you: Your name, website and the chains you launch on (Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain, Base and HyperEVM are supported). Either a token endpoint that answers whether an address is one of your launches and names its creator (and ideally the creation block), or your factory or hook contract address per chain with the signature of the event it emits at creation and where the token and creator sit in it. Optionally the address of the pool or pool manager that holds a launch’s liquidity, so it is labelled on the map. Send these to hello@gullylabs.xyz. Gully Labs adds the entry, checks it against live launches and replies when it is live. We take contract addresses only from you or from your deployments; we never guess them.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: Privacy-friendly web analytics with Web3 tracking for dapps: page views plus wallet connects, chain switches and transactions. It is a fork of Umami; everything Umami does still works. Gully Analytics: sign up with a wallet, install the tracker, Web3 events, address privacy modes, plans and what happens at the quota or when a plan lapses.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: Open the app dashboard, connect a wallet and sign the sign-in message (no transaction, no gas). In the Analytics tab press Start free trial. The server creates a Gully Analytics login for your wallet and shows its password once; copy it. We do not keep the password. Reset password in the same tab sets a new one and signs out open sessions. Add a website with its name and domain. The tab shows its website id, the install snippet, a link to its dashboard and the events counted this month. The free trial runs once per wallet. After it, choose a plan in the same tab to keep recording.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: The quickest way in is Open Gully Analytics in the Analytics tab of the app dashboard. It signs you straight in to the dashboard, with no password to type: the portal asks the server for a one-time sign-in link (POST /api/developer/analytics/sso), and the browser opens it on analytics.gullylabs.xyz. The link works once and only for 60 seconds, from the browser that asked for it. Only a hash of it is kept. Owners, admins and developers of the workspace can use it; billing members and viewers cannot. Everyone in the workspace opens the same Gully Analytics account. It never shows, changes or resets the account’s password, so a password you saved keeps working. The password login at analytics.gullylabs.xyz/login still works for anyone with the password. Forgot it? Reset password in the portal’s Analytics tab sets a new one.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: Put the snippet on every page, before the closing head tag. The Analytics tab gives it with your website id filled in. Without data-web3="true" the script behaves exactly like the Umami tracker. The usual Umami attributes (data-domains, data-do-not-track, data-tag, data-before-send, …) still apply, and Web3 events respect them.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: The script finds wallets through EIP-6963 and window.ethereum and watches what your dapp asks of them. It never calls a wallet method itself, so it cannot trigger a wallet prompt. All four events are standard custom events with event data, so they also show under Events, Goals, Funnels and filters. chainId is a decimal number; wallet is the wallet’s EIP-6963 id (io.metamask, io.rabby, …) or its name. You can send these events yourself too, and the Web3 dashboard reads them the same:

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: data-web3-address decides what is stored about the wallet address: hash (default) (counted): The first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the lowercase address. Wallets can be counted; the address cannot be read back. full (counted): The lowercase address. none (not counted): Nothing. Unique wallets and transactions per wallet show 0 or a dash. Hashing needs a secure context (HTTPS or localhost); on plain HTTP the address is dropped rather than sent in clear. A hash of a public address is pseudonymous, not anonymous: anyone with a candidate address can hash it and compare. Use none if that matters for your users.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: The plans below are read live from GET /api/plans (field analytics), the same source the pricing page and the dashboard use. An event is any call the tracker makes for one of your websites: page views, custom events and Web3 events. They are counted across your websites per calendar month in UTC. At the limit, new events are not recorded until the month turns or you upgrade. The tracker gets an HTTP 402 answer and stops sending for the rest of that page view. Websites beyond what your plan includes (after a downgrade, say) do not record until you remove some or upgrade; the oldest ones keep recording. Paying works like the tracker API plans (see Paying): USDC, USDT or the chain's own coin on Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, OP Mainnet, Polygon or Avalanche (where the treasury is deployed), straight to the treasury, checked on chain. A payment buys days; paying again for the same plan adds them to the end. Nothing renews by itself. When a trial or plan ends, recording stops. Your dashboard stays readable for days; after that the account and its data may be deleted.

chunks.title: Gully Analytics
chunks.text: Sign in at analytics.gullylabs.xyz with the login from the Analytics tab. Each website has the usual Umami views plus a Web3 tab: unique wallets, connects, connect rate, transactions, transactions per wallet, a visit → connect → transaction funnel, chains, wallet apps and the top pages by connects. The Umami REST API works with your own login: sign in with POST /api/auth/login and send the token as Authorization: Bearer …. The Web3 figures are at GET /api/websites/{websiteId}/web3?startAt=…&endAt=…. The source is public: gully-labs/umami, MIT licensed like Umami.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Non-custodial crypto billing: every payment is a plain transfer from the payer’s wallet straight to the treasury, read back from the chain. Invoices, reusable pay links, a hosted checkout and signed webhooks. Gully Pay: invoices and reusable pay links in USDC, USDT or the chain's own coin on seven chains, wallet QR codes, the Pay with crypto button, and signed merchant webhooks with how to verify them.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: An invoice (/pay/inv_…) asks for one US dollar amount. The payer picks a chain and an asset and gets a quote: the exact amount to send, valid for 20 minutes. Stablecoins count one to one with a unique tag in the last digits; the chains' own coins (ETH, BNB, POL, AVAX) are priced by the Chainlink USD feed on the same chain. A payment is checked on chain (success, right chain, right asset, the treasury, the exact amount, enough confirmations, never used before) before the invoice is marked paid. The same rules as API plans apply. Base (8453) (10): USDC (6 decimals), ETH Ethereum (1) (6): USDC, USDT (6 decimals), ETH BNB Chain (56) (15): USDT, USDC (18 decimals), BNB Arbitrum (42161) (10): USDC (6 decimals), ETH OP Mainnet (10) (10): USDC, USDT (6 decimals), ETH Polygon (137) (64): USDC (6 decimals), POL Avalanche (43114) (2): USDC, USDT (6 decimals), AVAX The live list, read from GET /api/plans as you look at this page (hover a chain for its assets and confirmations): Nothing is held in between: the transfer goes to the treasury in the payer’s own transaction. If no treasury is configured, every page says checkout is closed and shows no amount or QR.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: The treasury is a Safe: the same address on every chain, but it only exists on a chain where it has been deployed. The server reads eth_getCode(treasury) on every chain at start and hourly; a chain where the treasury has no code is not offered (no quote, no pay link, no checkout, no QR) until the Safe is deployed there, when it switches on by itself. The live list above is already filtered this way. Merchant payments go to the merchant's own wallet (checked the same way, per chain). The Gully Pay fee on a stablecoin payment is collected inside that payment through Request Network's ERC20FeeProxy only on a chain where that contract is verified byte for byte and the treasury is deployed; everywhere else, and for coin payments, the payer makes one plain transfer and the fee is invoiced to the merchant weekly. The payer never sees a difference in the amount. The server checks it; the page cannot change it. assets (string[]): Which chain and asset pairs it takes (all by default). active (boolean): Switched off links take no payments. expiresAt (date | null): After it, the link takes no payments. maxUses (number | null): How many paid uses it allows. chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Stablecoin payments to a store carry Gully Labs’ fee in the same transaction through Request Network’s ERC20FeeProxy, an immutable contract with no owner. It never holds tokens: one call moves the payment from the payer to the recipient and the fee to the treasury, and returns. The only way funds could end up inside it is a transfer sent straight to the proxy’s address, and nobody, Gully Labs included, could get those back. So the server and the checkout make that impossible: Every quote, QR code, wallet link, recipient address and split call passes one validator before it leaves the server. A proxy address (on any chain) is never a recipient; a split calls the proxy only through transferFromWithReferenceAndFee with zero value, an allowed stablecoin, the recipient and the treasury as the two legs and an approval for exactly the amount. Anything else answers 500 with no payment details at all. The Pay with wallet button checks the same rules again in the browser, simulates the proxy call with eth_call before your wallet sees it, and refuses to send on any failure. It never sends coin to the proxy and never falls back to a plain transfer to it. An hourly monitor reads every proxy’s balances on every chain. A non-zero balance (a transfer someone sent to the proxy by hand) alerts the Gully Labs team, who cannot recover it either but can warn the payer. Pay with the wallet button or send to the address shown on the quote. Never copy the pay.to contract address of a split into a wallet as a recipient: a plain transfer to it is lost for good, and the server names such a transaction as an unrecoverable mis-send instead of a payment.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Every quote carries an uri: an EIP-681 payment request for the exact amount, built on the server from base units (never floating point). The QR encodes it. Wallet support for EIP-681 varies: some read only the address, some ignore the amount or the chain. The checkout always shows the address, the exact amount and the token contract with copy buttons. Check the amount and the network in the wallet before sending.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Paste this on any site to send buyers to a pay link or an invoice. The link alone opens the checkout in a new tab; the optional script opens it in a popup window. The admin shows the snippet for each link and invoice. The checkout cannot be put in an iframe: its pages send frame-ancestors limited to Gully Labs itself, so wallet prompts and the address bar stay visible to the payer.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: A pay link, an invoice, or a default endpoint for everything else can have a webhook. When an invoice has its own, or its link has one, events go there; otherwise to the default, if set. invoice.paid (The payment is confirmed and the invoice marked paid.): invoice, link, payment invoice.expired (An open invoice ran out without a payment.): invoice, link invoice.cancelled (Gully Labs cancelled the invoice; it can no longer be paid. A cancelled invoice never sends invoice.expired afterwards.): invoice, link webhook.test (The admin pressed Send test event.): target, message https only. No user name or password in the URL. The host must resolve only to public addresses: private, loopback, link-local and reserved ranges are refused, and the request goes to the address that was checked. The signing secret (whsec_…) is shown once, when the endpoint is set. Rotating it shows the new one once; the old one stops at once. Five-second timeout, redirects not followed, the response body is not read.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: Every request carries two headers. The signature is an HMAC-SHA256, with your secret, of the timestamp, a dot, and the raw body: X-Gully-Timestamp (unix seconds): When it was sent. Refuse old ones (five minutes) to stop replays. X-Gully-Signature (sha256=<hex>): hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`)) It is the same scheme as gap alerts, so one verifier serves both.

chunks.title: Gully Pay
chunks.text: The first attempt goes out at once. Any answer other than 2xx, a timeout or a network error is retried after 1, 5, 10, 20 and 30 minutes: six attempts over about an hour. Then the delivery is marked failed. Retries carry the same event id and body; each is signed again with the current secret and timestamp. The queue is stored on disk, so a restart loses nothing: attempts that came due while the server was down go out when it is back. Each link and invoice shows its delivery log in the admin: event, state, attempts, last answer. A finished delivery (failed or delivered) can be redelivered from the admin, for example after your endpoint was down for longer than the retries. The same event goes out again, with the same id and body, as a new delivery with its own six attempts. Your handler should already drop an id it has handled. Events may arrive out of order and, rarely, more than once. Treat invoice.paid as the source of truth for a sale and look the invoice up by id.

The payer sends a plain transfer from their wallet to yours, in their own transaction. We read it back from a public node of that chain. Nothing passes through an account of ours, and we cannot move, hold or refund a payment.

chunks.text: A Safe (the multisig from safe.global) is a good store wallet: several owners, a threshold, no single key. One thing to know: a Safe exists only on the chains where it was deployed. Its address is the same everywhere, but on a chain where nobody deployed it there is no contract behind it, and a payment sent there is lost. That is why a chain stays off until the Safe has code on it. Deploy Safe on <chain>. A wallet row that reads “not deployed” has this button. Only if that address is exactly your Safe's do we offer the call; the page recomputes it once more before your wallet is asked. Your wallet signs. Connect any wallet with a little of the chain's coin for gas (about 240,000 gas; the estimate is shown first). It does not have to be a Safe owner. The transaction goes from your wallet to Safe's factory; Gully Labs never holds a key and never sends anything.

chunks.text: Scan contracts and code from the app, read the findings with their locations and draft proofs of concept, and ask people for a Security Review when a scan is not enough. Live today: the AI Security Scan, the Gully Score and contract monitors. Gully Security: the AI Security Scan (live; an AI review only for now), reading and publishing a report, the Gully Score and monitors, and requesting a human Security Review (quoted on request). chunks.title: Gully Security
chunks.text: AI Security Scan (live): automated and self-serve, in the app. For now it is an AI review only: our static-tools worker is not running yet, so Slither, Aderyn and fuzzing do not run, and every report says so in its label and lists those tools as not run. Every report says so. Gully Labs has not audited any project.

chunks.title: Gully Security
chunks.text: Open the Security page of the app and follow the five steps: choose the input, confirm the scope and the cost, pay if the free quota is used up, watch it run, read the report. Deployed contract (address + chain): Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, OP Mainnet, Polygon, BNB Chain or Avalanche; the verified source is read from the chain. Smart contract repo (owner/name + commit): A public GitHub repository; leave the commit empty for the default branch (the report names the exact commit it scanned). Upload (.zip of Solidity files, or one.sol): Web2 repo (owner/name + commit): A JavaScript or TypeScript backend on GitHub: a checklist scan, not a penetration test. A scan moves through queued, fetching, analysing, triaging and reporting to done (or failed with the reason, or cancelled if you stop it). The app shows each step live with the engine's own step text and an estimate of the time left. You can leave the page; the scan keeps running. Asking for a target you are already scanning shows that scan instead of starting another.

chunks.title: Gully Security
chunks.text: A paid scan gets a Gully Pay invoice, payable in the app or at its /pay/… page in USDC, USDT or the chain's own coin, straight to the Gully Labs treasury. The scan starts by itself once the payment is confirmed. If the price changes between your confirmation and the request (say a teammate used the last free scan), the app asks you to confirm again.

Findings by severity (critical, high, medium, low, info; severity is likelihood × impact) as a donut and bars; click one to filter the list. Each finding expands to its description, code location (file and line, with the snippet when the engine gives one), recommendation and status. A proof of concept where the engine could write one, labelled “Draft, not executed” unless the scanner ran it. Every finding is marked not verified by a human. The PoC code is visible to your workspace only. Every tool that ran, and every tool that did not, with the reason.
