chunks.title: Gully Score
chunks.text: The Gully Score is a 0 to 100 reading of how a contract is controlled and how it has behaved, built only from public evidence. Every part is shown with its weight, its source, a plain reason and a link to the evidence. How the Gully Score is worked out: every component, its weight and source, what happens when data is missing, monitoring alerts, the badge and widget, and why nobody can pay to change a score.

chunks.title: Gully Score
chunks.text: Each contract has a public page at /score/<chain>/<address> on gullylabs.xyz/score, with the score, the parts that went into it, its history and a log of every change. A score is read again when it is more than six hours old, and soon after Gully Security monitoring sees a privileged change on the contract. Scores are informational. They are not an endorsement and not investment advice. A high score says the public evidence looks good; it does not say a contract is safe.

chunks.title: Gully Score
chunks.text: The weights below are read live from the score service, the same numbers every score page uses. The score is the weighted average of the parts that could be read. Code verified: a full Sourcify match scores 100, a partial match 85, no published source 0. Who controls it: nobody (ownership given up) or a Safe needing two or more signatures 100, a timelock 80, an unrecognised contract 50, a Safe any one signer can use 40, a single wallet 15. Delay on changes: two days or more 100, one day 90, six hours 60, anything shorter 40, none 0. Can the code change: fixed code 100, upgradeable 30. Recent privileged changes: 100 less 25 for each change in the last 30 days. Liquidity locked: the share of the launch pools with a lock record, for DeepCore launches. Holder spread: the Holder Map’s Launch Health, or from the top-10 share (20% or less is 100, 90% or more is 0). Gully Security review: 100 less 40 per critical, 20 per high, 5 per medium and 1 per low finding (unresolved ones when the report says). Age: a year or more 100, six months 85, three months 70, a month 50, a week 30, younger 10.

chunks.title: Gully Score
chunks.text: Sourcify is the primary source for "Code verified". It recompiles the published source and compares it with the code on chain, and anyone can repeat that check. A full match means the compiled code and its metadata match exactly; a partial match means the code matches but the metadata (comments, file names) differs. The part names which one it is and links to the contract on sourcify.dev. Etherscan is asked only when Sourcify has no match, and only where an Etherscan key is configured. Gully Security scans read source in the same order. Gully Labs verifies the contracts it deploys and relies on there too: the list, with each status, is in contracts/CHOICE.md.

chunks.title: Gully Score
chunks.text: When a part cannot be read (the contract is not verified anywhere we can check, nobody watches it with monitoring, it is not a DeepCore launch, the Holder Map does not cover its chain) the page shows the part as not available, says why, and leaves its weight out. It is never scored as zero. With less than of the 100 weight points available there is no score at all, only the parts.

chunks.title: Gully Score
chunks.text: The score is worked out from a chain and an address and nothing else. No plan, payment, account or workspace is read, so no plan can move it. A Gully Security review counts only once its report is published, and the page links to it with its finding counts. A draft or private report counts for nothing. There is no badge to buy. Watching a contract with monitoring, on any plan, adds the “recent privileged changes” part for everyone, good or bad. Choosing whether a watched contract is listed on /score does not change its score.

chunks.title: Gully Score
chunks.text: In the app’s Security tab, a workspace adds a contract (chain and address). It is read every minute through our RPC failover: owner, admin and role changes, upgrades (ERC-1967 and beacon proxies, and a change of the code address found by reading it directly), pauses, signer and threshold changes on the Safe that controls it, and large outflows of its own tokens or coin over the share or amount you set. Each alert is one plain line with a link, sent to Telegram and/or your webhook, and never twice: an event is marked as sent on disk before it goes out, so a restart resumes where it stopped without repeating anything. How many contracts a workspace can watch is part of its plan (pricing). The load is small: about three RPC calls a minute per chain in use, shared by every contract on it, plus about one call a minute per contract.

chunks.title: Gully Score
chunks.text: Every score page has a badge (an SVG with the score and the date it was read, in the Gully Labs kit) and a live widget. Both link back to the score page, where every part and its evidence is shown.

chunks.title: Gully Score
chunks.text: Public, read-only and open to any origin. A contract that has not been scored before is worked out on the first request (a few seconds), within a per-address rate limit.

chunks.title: Gully AI
chunks.text: An assistant that answers questions about Gully Labs from our own docs and live data, cites where every fact came from, and says “I don’t know” when it does not. How Gully AI answers questions about Gully Labs: its sources and citations, the live tools it reads, where it runs (site, ⌘K, docs, app, Telegram), its limits and what it logs.

chunks.title: Gully AI
chunks.text: Gully AI answers questions about Gully Labs and its products: the stock token tracker and its API, the widget, API keys, plans and alerts, the Holder Map, Gully Analytics, Gully Pay and merchant stores, Chain Kit, the roadmap, DeepCore, the Telegram bot, privacy and the services we offer. It describes; it never advises. It does not predict prices or gaps, and never says whether to buy, sell or hold anything. It never invents a price, fee, limit, date, address or link. A figure that is not in a source or a tool result is not given. When the sources do not cover a question it searches once more in other words, then says plainly that it does not know and points to these docs or the contact form. Answers are short: a few plain sentences or a short list. Live figures appear as a card under the answer.

chunks.title: Gully AI
chunks.text: What this server reports about Gully AI right now, and how quickly the status endpoint answers your browser. Below it, the server’s own 24-hour check of Gully AI from the status page.

chunks.title: Gully AI
chunks.text: Every answer is built from numbered sources: passages of these docs, the main site, the changelog, the legal pages, the roadmap, the Gully Pay contract notes, the Telegram bot and Mini App, our public READMEs and the blog. Each sentence that states a fact carries its source number, like [1], and the sources are listed as links under the answer. Retrieval is hybrid when semantic search is configured: keyword search (BM25) on your question and on a synonym-expanded version of it, plus nearest passages by meaning, fused and re-ranked. Without it the mode is BM25: keyword search with synonyms. The panel above shows which one this server uses. A fact read live from a tool is cited with a label like [L1] and the time it was read.

chunks.title: Gully AI
chunks.text: For anything that changes, Gully AI reads live data first, even when a page seems to cover it. At most three rounds of tool calls happen per answer. get_stock (everyone): One stock token’s latest tracker reading: onchain and fair price, gap, status, pool liquidity, feed session get_top_gaps (everyone): The widest trusted gaps right now get_ledger (everyone): The live figures of the Gully Labs projects, as each venue publishes them deepcore_launches (everyone): The newest or most traded DeepCore launches, with when they were read deepcore_pool (everyone): One token’s DeepCore pools: price, liquidity, lock, swaps get_holders (everyone): A token’s Holder Map in summary: top-10 share, clusters, the launch checks get_plans (everyone): Current plans, limits, payment chains and whether checkout is open get_pay_chains (everyone): What Gully Pay accepts on which chain, and the confirmations needed get_alert_channels (everyone): Which alert delivery channels this server offers search_docs (everyone): Searches the docs, site and blog again in other words get_my_store (signed in): Your own Gully Pay store, in your active workspace get_my_usage (signed in): Your own API usage and plan, in your active workspace get_my_alerts (signed in): Your own alerts, in your active workspace The “my” tools take no workspace from the question: the workspace comes from your signed-in session in the app, never from the model. Signed out, they refuse, and the answer says to sign in to the app.

chunks.title: Gully AI
chunks.text: gullylabs.xyz/ask, the full page. The launcher on the site and in these docs: the “Ask” button in the top bar, or ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux). The app dashboard at app.gullylabs.xyz, where a signed-in session unlocks the “my” tools for your active workspace. The Telegram bot: /ask <question> or the Gully AI button in @GullyLabsBot. A private chat linked to a wallet gets that wallet’s workspace; a group never does. See the Telegram bot page.

chunks.title: Gully AI
chunks.text: Question length (500 characters): Longer questions are refused with a 400 Request body (16 KB): Larger requests get a 413 Conversation history (last 4 turns): Each turn trimmed to 600 characters Per visitor (6 a minute, 60 a day): Counted per IP address; a 429 says when to try again Per Telegram chat (5 a minute, 60 a day): Counted per chat Whole service (2,000 answers a day): Across every surface; the spending cap The owner can change these on the server. When Gully AI is not configured on a server, every surface says it is not available (the API answers 503 with configured: false).

chunks.title: Gully AI
chunks.text: Questions are logged for 90 days to find gaps in these docs. The log never holds a raw IP address: only a salted hash of it. A thumbs up or down keeps the answer id, the rating, the question and the same hash, also for 90 days. Retrieved text and tool results are treated as data, not instructions: they are wrapped in blocks tagged with a random id per request, and any instruction inside them is ignored. Gully AI is information only. It is not investment, financial, legal or tax advice. The full policy is at gullylabs.xyz/legal/privacy.

chunks.title: Gully AI
chunks.text: GET /api/ask/status answers { configured, model, indexSize, updatedAt, retrieval }. POST /api/ask takes { question, history? } and needs the header X-Requested-With: gully; it answers { id, answer, citations, live, cards, actions, usedTools, model, signedIn }. Send Accept: text/event-stream to get progress events before the answer. POST /api/ask/feedback with { id, rating: 'up' | 'down' } rates an answer from the last 24 hours.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: @GullyLabsBot puts the tracker, DeepCore launches, your alerts and Gully AI in Telegram, with a Mini App for the full screens. The @GullyLabsBot Telegram bot and its Mini App: commands, menus, gap and launch alerts with Mute, connecting a chat from the app, the @GullyLabsNews channel requirement, groups and announcements.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: Looks up any stock token the tracker follows, on Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain and Solana, with its gap to the fair price and a 24-hour sparkline. Lists the widest gaps now and the biggest gap moves over 24 hours and one hour. Shows the newest DeepCore launches, per chain, and can alert you to new ones. Delivers your gap, launch and Holder Map alerts, and lets you pause, mute, test or delete them. Answers questions through Gully AI. A figure the bot could not read is called unreadable, never shown as zero.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: Which alert channels this server offers right now, and the server’s own check of the bot’s webhook over the last 24 hours (Telegram’s getWebhookInfo: updates waiting and the last delivery error). The full picture is on the Status page.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: Using the bot’s menus, commands, Gully AI and the Mini App requires following @GullyLabsNews, our news channel. Without it the bot shows a “Join @GullyLabsNews” button and an “I’ve joined” button that checks again. Alert deliveries and their Mute buttons always work, followed or not: alerts are part of a service you may have paid for. So do the ways out: listing, pausing and deleting your own alerts, and stopping announcements. If Telegram cannot tell the bot whether you follow the channel, the bot lets you through rather than locking you out.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: The Menu button next to the text box lists these. Each one opens the matching screen. /start (private): The main menu (with a code from the app: links this chat) /app (private): Opens the Mini App /gap NVDA (private, groups): One stock token’s card /top (private, groups): The tokens furthest from their real share price /movers (private): Biggest gap moves in 24 hours /launches (private, groups): Newest tokens launched on DeepCore /alerts (private): Your alerts: pause, mute, test or delete /ask (private): Ask Gully AI a question /help (private, groups): What the bot does /stop (private): Stop announcements, or unlink this chat /menu still works when typed; it is the same screen as /start.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: The bot is menu-driven: each screen is one message, edited in place as you tap. The main menu leads to: Stocks: pick a chain, then a ticker (or search), then the stock card with its 24-hour sparkline and a step-by-step alert maker (threshold, then direction: premium, discount or both). Top gaps and Movers (24 h or 1 h). DeepCore launches: filter by chain, open a launch, set a new-launch alert, or open its Holder Map. My alerts: pause, resume, mute for 24 hours, send a test, or delete. Gully AI: type a question, or tap an example. Answers arrive as new messages so the next screen never overwrites them. Settings: mute every alert for 24 hours, usage notices on or off, announcements on or off, unlink this chat.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: Alerts belong to a wallet account in the app. You connect a Telegram chat to it once, with no chat id to copy: Open the app at app.gullylabs.xyz, go to Alerts and choose Connect Telegram. The app makes a one-time code (valid for 10 minutes, usable once; only its hash is stored) and opens the bot with it. Press Start. The bot confirms the link. New alerts deliver to that chat by default. One chat per account: a newer link replaces the older one. /stop or Settings → Unlink removes it. Alerts follow the same plan limits as in the app; see Plans & alerts.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: Gap alerts, DeepCore new-launch alerts and Holder Map alerts are created in the app, the bot or the Mini App, all through the same rules. Each delivery carries a Mute 24h button that silences that alert for a day; Settings can mute every alert at once. Sending respects Telegram’s own limits (about one message a second per chat), so a burst of alerts arrives spread out rather than dropped.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: The Mini App is the Gully app inside Telegram, at gullylabs.xyz/tg. Open it from the “📱 Open app” button on the main menu, from /app, or from the bot profile’s Open app button. Gaps: every tracked token across chains with its 24-hour gap line. Stock: a 24-hour chart and an alert composer; Telegram’s main button creates the alert. Launches: DeepCore launches per chain, each with its Holder Map. My alerts: your linked account’s alerts, to pause, resume, test or delete. Holders: a token’s Holder Map, opened from the bot’s “👥 Holders” button. It follows your Telegram theme. Every request is signed with the data Telegram gives the app, checked on our server and refused when older than 24 hours; nothing is stored as a session. The News channel requirement applies here too, with the same exits left open. More: Telegram Mini App.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: Add the bot to a group to use /gap, /top, /launches and /help there. Telegram does not allow the Mini App button in groups. A group can receive alerts: link it with a code from the app the same way. Only the person who linked a group can unlink it, or create, pause, mute, test or delete alerts there. Gully AI never reads a workspace from a group.

chunks.title: Telegram bot
chunks.text: When you start the bot in a private chat we record when you first and last used it, your language, whether the chat is linked, whether you follow the News channel as last read, and whether you opted out of announcements. Occasional announcements go to private chats only; “🔕 Stop announcements” on any of them, or /stop announcements, turns them off. That never stops your alerts. Details are in the privacy policy at gullylabs.xyz/legal/privacy.

chunks.title: Telegram Mini App
chunks.text: The Mini App is the Gully app inside Telegram: the gap list, one stock with an alert composer, DeepCore launches, a token’s Holder Map and your alerts. It belongs to @GullyLabsBot. The Gully Labs Telegram Mini App at gullylabs.xyz/tg: how it opens, its screens, how each request is signed with Telegram's initData, the /api/tg routes, rate limits and errors.

chunks.title: Telegram Mini App
chunks.text: The app is served at gullylabs.xyz/tg and only works inside Telegram. In a normal browser it shows “Open this inside Telegram” with a link to the bot and to the tracker. Inside Telegram it opens from: the “📱 Open app” button on the bot’s main menu (private chats only: Telegram does not allow this button type in groups); the /app command in a private chat; the “👥 Holders” button under a token, which opens that token’s Holder Map screen directly. A Holder Map screen can also be opened with /tg?holders=<chain>:<token>, or with a Telegram start parameter of the form h_<chain>_<token>. Anything malformed is ignored and the app opens on its home screen. The app expands to full height, follows your Telegram theme (colours are mapped onto the site’s tokens and change live when you switch day and night mode), uses Telegram’s Back button to leave a stock or Holder Map screen, and gives haptic feedback on taps where the device supports it.

chunks.title: Telegram Mini App
chunks.text: Gaps (home tab): Every tracked stock token across chains, filterable by chain, each with a 24-hour gap line. Tap one to open it. Stock (from Gaps): A 24-hour gap chart for the token, its status in plain words, and an alert composer. A Holder Map shortcut shows only on chains where the Holder Map has data. Launches (home tab): The latest DeepCore launches, filtered by All, BNB, HyperEVM, Robinhood or Base, each with a link to DeepCore and to its Holder Map, plus a new-launch alert. My alerts (home tab): The linked account’s alerts with the plan limit, to pause, resume, test or delete. Also the switch for Gully Labs announcements in your private chat. Holders (from a launch, a stock or the bot): The token’s Holder Map in compact form, and an alert for when its largest connected cluster reaches 10%, 20% or 30%. Gaps and statuses come from the same data as the tracker. A token without enough trading says so in words rather than showing a gap. The 24-hour lines come from GET /api/tg/sparks.

chunks.title: Telegram Mini App
chunks.text: Alerts belong to a wallet account in the main app. A Telegram user is mapped to the account linked to their private chat with the bot (or, failing that, a group they linked). Until a chat is linked the app shows “not linked”, and creating an alert opens the app dashboard instead; see connecting a chat. Gap alert: on a stock screen, pick a threshold from 0.1 to 100 percent and a direction (above, below or both). Telegram’s main button at the bottom creates it, and it delivers to your linked chat. New-launch alert: on the Launches screen, for one DeepCore chain or any. Holder Map alert: on a Holders screen, when the largest connected cluster holds at least the chosen share. Alerts are created through the same code as the dashboard, so its validation and your plan’s limits apply, and the app shows the server’s own sentence when it refuses. See Plans & alerts. An account blocked from the developer programme cannot create or change alerts.

chunks.title: Telegram Mini App
chunks.text: Every call to /api/tg/* carries the raw initData string Telegram gives the app, in the header Authorization: tma <initData>. The server checks it the way Telegram’s documentation describes: an HMAC-SHA256 over the sorted fields, keyed from the bot token, compared in constant time. It is refused when it is missing, longer than 4,096 characters, has no valid hash, repeats a field, has no user, or belongs to a bot. It is refused when its auth_date is older than 24 hours or more than five minutes in the future. An expired session shows “This session has expired”: close the app and open it again. Nothing is stored as a session and no cookie is set, so there is nothing to carry across sites.

chunks.title: Telegram Mini App
chunks.text: These routes exist for the Mini App and need Telegram’s signed initData, so they cannot be called from a script of your own. They are listed so you can see what the app does. GET /api/tg/me (Your Telegram user, the News channel status (gate), the linked account (shortened), the dashboard link, whether announcements are on, and the chains that have Holder Map data.): ?fresh=1 re-reads channel membership POST /api/tg/announcements (Body { on: boolean }. Turns Gully Labs announcements in your private chat on or off.): 20 a minute; never gated GET /api/tg/sparks (Each tracked token’s last 24 hours of gap, thinned to about 24 points, keyed chain:TICKER.): cached a minute GET /api/tg/launches (Up to 20 latest DeepCore launches, optionally ?chain=<id> (56, 999, 4663 or 8453).): 400 for another chain id GET /api/tg/alerts (The linked account’s alerts and plan limits, each alert with its last three deliveries.): never gated POST /api/tg/alerts (Creates a gap alert, a Holder Map alert (kind: holders) or a new-launch alert (kind: deepcore-launch), all delivered to Telegram.): 30 changes a minute POST /api/tg/alerts/:id/(pause|resume|test|delete) (Changes one alert.): pause and delete never gated

chunks.title: Telegram Mini App
chunks.text: 401 (initData missing, invalid or expired): The body carries the reason. Reopen the app. 403 (You do not follow the News channel, or the account is blocked from the developer programme): For the channel the body also carries gate. 404 (The Mini App is not configured on this server, or an unknown route): Nothing to retry. 409 (Alerts without a linked chat): The body has linkNeeded and the dashboard link. 429 (Over 120 requests a minute per Telegram user, 30 alert changes, or 20 announcement changes): Wait a moment and try again.

chunks.title: Telegram Mini App
chunks.text: Following @GullyLabsNews is required to use the app. Without it you get a join screen with a Join button and an “I’ve joined” button. Listing, pausing and deleting your alerts, and the announcements switch, keep working. The details are on the News channel gate page.

chunks.title: News channel gate
chunks.text: To use the bot’s features you follow @GullyLabsNews, our news channel. The gate only guards new feature use. Anything that stops, mutes or removes something you already set up stays open. Why the Gully Labs Telegram bot and Mini App ask you to follow @GullyLabsNews, how membership is checked and cached, and everything that stays open without it: alerts, Mute, pausing, deleting and unlinking.

chunks.title: News channel gate
chunks.text: Menus, commands, Gully AI and the Mini App need you to follow the channel. If you do not, the bot answers with “Follow Gully Labs News to use this bot” and two buttons: Join the channel, and “✅ I’ve joined”, which checks again straight away. When the check passes, the main menu opens. The channel is set on the server by TELEGRAM_REQUIRED_CHANNEL: @GullyLabsNews by default, and the value off disables the gate.

chunks.title: News channel gate
chunks.text: The bot asks Telegram (getChatMember) whether you are the channel’s creator, an administrator or a member, or a restricted user who is still a member. Anything else counts as not following. You follow (30 minutes): So every tap is not a call to Telegram. You do not follow (20 seconds): So joining takes effect almost at once. You tap “I’ve joined” (checked fresh): The remembered answer is skipped for that check. The result is also kept with your bot-user record (whether you follow, as last read), as described in the privacy section of the Telegram bot page.

chunks.title: News channel gate
chunks.text: Alert deliveries and their Mute buttons always work, followed or not. Alerts are part of a service you may have paid for, and someone who leaves the channel must still be able to stop what they set up. Also open without the channel: listing your alerts (/alerts) and pausing, resuming, muting, testing or deleting them, and muting all of them; Gully Security monitor alerts and their Mute buttons (/monitors); Settings: unlinking a chat, and switching announcements or usage notices off; /stop; linking a chat with /start and a code from the app. Creating a new alert, opening a stock, the top gaps, launches and Gully AI wait for the channel. A first /start in a private chat is still recorded before the gate answers.

chunks.title: News channel gate
chunks.text: In a group the bot ignores ordinary chatter and only reacts to its own commands. A member who does not follow gets the join screen at most once every 30 minutes, so one person’s commands do not fill the group; their other commands are dropped quietly in between. Pressing a button in a group gets a short “Follow Gully Labs News first” notice instead of a message.

chunks.title: News channel gate
chunks.text: The Mini App applies the same gate on the server. GET /api/tg/me reports whether you follow, and the app shows the join screen with Join and “I’ve joined” (which re-reads membership fresh). Every feature route answers 403 with the gate details until you follow. The exits stay open: GET /api/tg/alerts, pausing and deleting an alert, and the announcements switch. If your chat is linked, the join screen lists your alerts with pause and delete so you can stop them without joining.

chunks.title: News channel gate
chunks.text: Telegram only answers membership questions for a channel when the bot is an administrator there. If the check itself fails (which is not the same as “not a member”), the bot lets people through rather than locking everyone out, and logs a warning for us, at most once every ten minutes. A broken gate never blocks you. See Telegram bot for commands and menus, and the live webhook check on Status.

chunks.title: Stock pages
chunks.text: Every token the tracker follows has its own page at gullylabs.xyz/tracker/<chain>/<TICKER>. It is everything the tracker knows about that one token, read live. Nothing on it is typed in by hand. What each tracked stock token's page on gullylabs.xyz/tracker shows: price against fair price, the gap and its change, pool depth and history, contracts, swap, alerts, the Holder Map and an embeddable badge.

chunks.title: Stock pages
chunks.text: Open a row in the tracker and you land on its page, for example /tracker/robinhood/NVDA. The chain keys are robinhood, bsc and solana. The same ticker on two chains has two pages, and each links to the other. The page also lists the other tokens on the same chain. Its data is the tracker’s: the page re-reads it every minute, and the figures animate to each new read. Where the tracker prices a token two ways, onchain from its deepest pool and fair from Chainlink or, for some Solana xStocks, the issuer’s quote, the page names the source. How that works is in the methodology.

chunks.title: Stock pages
chunks.text: Onchain (deepest pool): The token’s price in its deepest pool, with the pair it trades against. Fair (fair-price feed): The fair price, with who priced it and how old the read is. Gap (onchain vs fair): How far the onchain price is from fair. A thin pool is labelled “thin pool, not trusted”. Gap Δ 1h, Gap Δ 24h (/api/tracker/movers): How much the gap moved over the window, in percentage points, with the gap then and now. Liquidity, Volume 24h (deepest pool): The deepest pool’s liquidity and 24-hour volume. All pools (every pool found): How many pools the token has and their total liquidity. A status badge beside the title says where the token stands. The two change cells explain themselves when they have no value: “reading snapshots” while loading, “could not be read”, “not a trusted pool now” for a token that is not a trusted reading, or “needs 1h of snapshots” or “needs 24h of snapshots” while there is not enough history yet.

chunks.title: Stock pages
chunks.text: The gap chart shows the last 24 hours or 7 days, as the gap or as onchain against fair, from the tracker’s five-minute snapshots. You can drag to zoom, and the 7-day view adds a slider. Stretches without readings are marked on the chart. Below it, a footer names the pool, the fair-price method and whether the market is open. Pool depth shows the token’s deepest pool. The data behind the chart is the public GET /api/tracker/history; see the API reference.

chunks.title: Stock pages
chunks.text: Swap: a swap card for the token, through LI.FI on Robinhood Chain and BNB Chain and Jupiter on Solana. It stays closed where the region check says so. Your wallet signs everything; see Swaps. Contracts: the token, its fair-price feed (or the fair-price source) and its pool, each with a copy button and an explorer link (Blockscout, BscScan, Etherscan or Solscan, by chain). Follow: “Alert me when the gap moves” opens the app’s Alerts tab with this token ready in the new-alert dialog, a button that copies a live badge for your site, and the same token on other chains. The page also has a “Post on X” button that shares the token’s gap, and a link to the pool on DexScreener.

chunks.title: Stock pages
chunks.text: Below the cards the page embeds the token’s Holder Map. Where a token has no map, or a chain’s stock maps are not available yet, it says so instead of showing an empty map. A “How swaps work” block answers who runs the swap, custody, cost and who can use it, and the page ends with the note that it is information, not investment advice.

chunks.title: Stock pages
chunks.text: A value that could not be read shows a dash, never zero. If the whole tracker cannot be read the page says so. A ticker the tracker does not follow, or one on the wrong chain, answers 404 with a search instead of a silent redirect. A lower-case ticker redirects to the upper-case address (/tracker/bsc/aapl goes to /tracker/bsc/AAPL) if the token exists.

chunks.title: Stock pages
chunks.section: Put the badge on your site
chunks.text: The page’s “Copy a live badge for your site” button copies this snippet for that token. The options are in the widget guide.

chunks.title: Swaps
chunks.text: Each stock page can swap into or out of its token, right beside the gap. The routing is LI.FI on EVM chains and Jupiter on Solana; your own wallet signs every transaction. How swaps work on Gully Labs stock pages: LI.FI on Robinhood Chain and BNB Chain, Jupiter on Solana, the region check (GET /api/geo), the Jupiter proxy, fees, and why your wallet signs everything.

chunks.title: Swaps
chunks.text: Open a token from the tracker and its page has a swap card. On Robinhood Chain and BNB Chain it pays with the chain’s native coin (ETH or BNB) through LI.FI; on Solana it buys or sells the xStock with SOL or USDC through Jupiter. The card sits next to the live gap so you can see the fair price before you trade. Swaps are executed by third-party exchanges. The token is issued by a third party that can pause, block or change it; it tracks the stock but is not the share itself.

chunks.title: Swaps
chunks.text: How deep each token’s deepest pool is right now, from the tracker (the same pool its onchain price is read from). A shallow pool means more price impact on a swap. A token whose pool could not be read is counted, never drawn as zero.

chunks.title: Swaps
chunks.text: Three checks run before any swap code is even loaded: The token is on a chain we can route: Robinhood Chain or BNB Chain (LI.FI), or Solana (Jupiter). Your region may see it. The page asks GET /api/geo, which reads the country Cloudflare attaches to the request; no third-party geo service is called. The United States and comprehensively sanctioned countries (Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria) are not offered swaps. If the country cannot be told (no header, unknown, Tor), the swap is not shown; if the check itself fails, the page fails closed too. You tick “I understand” under a short notice. The tick is remembered in this browser only. A blocked or unknown region still sees the gap, a gap alert button and the pool on DexScreener: never a dead end. The country is a guess from the IP address, not identity.

chunks.title: Swaps
chunks.text: On Robinhood Chain and BNB Chain the card is the LI.FI widget, locked to the token’s chain and connected to the site’s own wallet connection. For comparison it also shows what DeepCore’s router would give for the same payment (read through our cached GET /api/deepcore/quote); “Swap on DeepCore” opens deepcore.fun, nothing is executed from here.

chunks.title: Swaps
chunks.text: On Solana the card asks this site for a Jupiter quote and an unsigned transaction, so the browser talks only to gullylabs.xyz. Your wallet signs and sends it. The proxy applies the same region check (it answers 451 where swaps are not offered), caches quotes and limits the rate: GET /api/solana/jupiter/quote (20 a minute per IP): A quote to buy the xStock with SOL or USDC, or sell it back; cached 10 s per pair and amount POST /api/solana/jupiter/swap (6 a minute per IP): Turns a quote (valid 60 s) into an unsigned transaction for your wallet: { quoteId, userPublicKey } Slippage (0.5%): Every quote states its minimum out and its price impact More on Solana coverage: Solana.

chunks.title: Swaps
chunks.text: Any fee Gully Labs adds is set by the owner on the server and stated in the quote before you confirm. Exchanges and networks charge their own fees and slippage on top. What this build of the site says: Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain (LI.FI): Solana (Jupiter): On Solana the fee and its recipient come from the same server-side record for the quote and the swap, so a page cannot ask for a different fee or recipient. A swap with no usable fee account carries no fee, and the quote says so.

chunks.title: Swaps
chunks.text: Gully Labs never holds your funds or your keys. Quotes and unsigned transactions come from LI.FI or Jupiter through our pages and proxy; your wallet signs and sends every transaction. Swaps are information and tooling, not investment advice.

chunks.title: Solana
chunks.text: Solana is the tracker’s third chain, beside Robinhood Chain and BNB Chain: xStocks are priced two ways like every other token, and Gully Pay accepts SOL, USDC and USDT. Gully Labs on Solana: xStocks in the tracker, fair prices from Chainlink or the issuer's quote, the Holder Map on Solana, Solana Pay in Gully Pay, and Jupiter swaps on stock pages.

chunks.title: Solana
chunks.text: Tracker: xStocks, Backed Finance’s tokenised stocks (SPL Token-2022), in the same row shape as the EVM chains, so history, movers, the heatmap, the bot’s /gap and /top, and gap alerts all work unchanged. Holder Map: the largest holders of each tracked xStock. Gully Pay: SOL, USDC and USDT through Solana Pay. Swaps: buy or sell an xStock with SOL or USDC through Jupiter, on its stock page.

chunks.title: Solana
chunks.text: Each xStock’s gap to its fair price as the tracker reads it now, coloured by who priced fair. Rows without a gap (no pool, an unreadable feed, an unverified print) are listed by name with their status, never charted as zero.

chunks.title: Solana
chunks.text: An xStock’s fair price is the underlying share’s price times the token’s own multiplier. xStocks carry Token-2022’s scaled UI amount extension: one token is multiplier shares (dividends raise it, splits multiply it). The multiplier is read from the mint every refresh, and a scheduled new one applies from its effective time. Chainlink equity feed on BNB Chain or Robinhood Chain (chainlink:56 / chainlink:4663): First choice: the same feeds the EVM rows use, read on chain Verified Chainlink feed on Ethereum (chainlink:1): When the share has a verified Ethereum feed The issuer’s quote (backed): When no Chainlink feed covers the share: Backed’s own xStocks API Each row names its source in fairSource, and follows its feed’s own session (NYSE hours for BNB Chain feeds, 24/5 for Robinhood and Ethereum feeds). Outside the session, the gap is against the last session’s price. Details: methodology.

chunks.title: Solana
chunks.text: DexScreener finds each token’s deepest pool (and reports liquidity and volume) once an hour. Between discoveries the price is read straight from the pool account when it is an Orca Whirlpool, a Raydium CLMM or a Meteora DLMM pool; each layout is checked against the pool’s own mints before it is believed. Any other pool keeps DexScreener’s price, labelled as an API reading with its time. The trust rules are the same as on every chain: a thin pool is never flagged, and an implausible gap is withheld as “unverified”.

chunks.title: Solana
chunks.text: For xStocks the Holder Map reads the 20 largest token accounts over the Solana RPC and merges them by owner; owners that are program accounts are marked as such. Links between wallets (who sent to whom) are not read on Solana yet, so a Solana map has no clusters. When this server has no Solana RPC configured, the map says holder data is not available rather than showing an empty one.

chunks.title: Solana
chunks.text: Gully Pay accepts SOL, USDC and USDT on Solana, with the same quotes, ledger and reuse rule as the EVM chains. Each quote is a Solana Pay transfer request with its own reference key, so a wallet that follows the spec lets us find the payment without you pasting a signature. A payment counts once its transaction is finalized and did not fail. SOL: the treasury’s own balance rose by the amount. USDC or USDT: the treasury’s associated token account for that mint rose by the amount, in that mint. SOL is priced by Chainlink’s SOL / USD feed (read on Arbitrum); an answer older than two hours gives no SOL quote. A signature can be used for one payment only, across every chain. Solana checkout is on only when the owner has set the Solana treasury wallet. Unset, Solana assets are not offered and every page says so. There is never a fallback address. The full flow is on the Solana Pay page.

chunks.title: Solana
chunks.text: On a Solana stock page the swap card uses Jupiter: buy the xStock with SOL or USDC, or sell it back. Quotes and the unsigned transaction come through our proxy, behind the same region check as every swap; your wallet signs it. See Swaps.

chunks.title: Solana
chunks.text: Pages talk to Solana only through this site. POST /api/solana/rpc is a narrow JSON-RPC proxy for wallet payments and swap status: it allows getLatestBlockhash, getSignatureStatuses, getBalance, getTokenAccountsByOwner, getAccountInfo (120 a minute per IP) and sendTransaction (10 a minute per IP). GET /api/solana/pay/find?quote=<id> lists signatures that touched a quote’s reference key (40 a minute per IP). Explorer links go to Solscan.

chunks.title: Solana Pay
chunks.text: Gully Pay takes SOL, USDC and USDT on Solana as Solana Pay transfer requests. Each quote has its own reference key, so a phone wallet that follows the spec pays from a QR code and the page finds the payment by itself. How Gully Pay takes SOL, USDC and USDT on Solana: the Solana Pay transfer request and its reference key, paying by QR, wallet or pasted signature, when a payment counts, the find endpoint and the refusals.

chunks.title: Solana Pay
chunks.text: Solana Pay works in Gully Labs’ own checkout: the quotes made for the pay page and the app’s checkout. It uses the same quotes, ledger and one-signature-one-payment rule as the EVM chains. Merchant stores take the EVM chains for now, so a store does not offer Solana. The specification is the Solana Pay transfer request. Solana as a whole (the tracker, Holder Map and swaps) is on the Solana page.

chunks.title: Solana Pay
chunks.text: USDC (SPL token, mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, 6 decimals): One USDC per dollar of the quote USDT (SPL token, mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, 6 decimals): One USDT per dollar of the quote SOL (A plain transfer of the coin, 9 decimals): Chainlink’s SOL / USD feed, read on Arbitrum The SOL feed is read through Arbitrum’s RPCs, because Chainlink’s SOL / USD price feed we use lives there. If the feed’s last answer is older than two hours, no SOL quote is given and the page suggests a stablecoin. The feed and its last answer are shown on the quote.

chunks.title: Solana Pay
chunks.text: The QR code on the pay page, and the link behind it, is a Solana Pay transfer request built on the server from the quote’s exact base units, so the amount is never rounded. reference is a fresh public key (32 random bytes) made for that one quote. A wallet that follows the spec adds it as a read-only account to the transfer, which is what lets us find the payment on chain. amount is a plain decimal with no exponent. Each open quote in an asset has a different amount, so an exact transfer names its quote; the unique part is in lamports for SOL. A quote lives 20 minutes, and a payment may be mined up to 10 minutes after it runs out.

chunks.title: Solana Pay
chunks.text: Scan the QR with a Solana Pay wallet. While the quote can still be paid, the page asks GET /api/solana/pay/find about every five seconds, and hands the first signature it sees to the normal check: “Payment seen on Solana: checking it now.” Pay with wallet: connect a Wallet Standard wallet in the browser and sign one transaction that pays the treasury the exact quoted amount and carries the quote’s reference. For USDC and USDT the transaction first creates the treasury’s token account if it is missing, and the payer covers its rent once (about 0.002 SOL). For SOL a small amount is kept back for the network fee. If the wallet does not hold enough, the page says so and nothing is sent. Paste the signature of a payment made from any wallet. It is the transaction signature (base58, 87 or 88 characters), not a 0x hash. The reference is optional here, because the quote’s exact amount already names it.

chunks.title: Solana Pay
chunks.text: The transaction is finalized, which takes about 15 seconds, and did not fail. Anything less answers “not finalized yet”: check again shortly. SOL: the treasury’s own balance rose by the amount. USDC or USDT: the treasury’s associated token account for that mint rose by the amount, in that mint, under the classic SPL Token program. A transfer to any other account or in any other mint does not count. The amount is at least the quote’s minimum, and a payment from a wallet other than the signed-in one must equal the quoted amount exactly. It falls inside the quote’s life: not made before the checkout was opened (two minutes of clock skew are allowed), and not mined more than 10 minutes after the quote ran out. The signature was never used before for any payment, on any chain. If an amount is short or cannot be matched, nothing is applied, and the message asks you to write to hello@gullylabs.xyz with the signature so the difference can be settled by hand.

chunks.title: Solana Pay
chunks.text: Lists the signatures that touched a quote’s reference key, newest first, at most 10, with failed transactions left out. It is what the pay page polls. It takes the quote’s id, and the answer says whether the quote is already marked paid. 200 (A Solana quote): reference, paid and signatures (possibly empty). 404 (An unknown quote, or one without a reference): There is no such Solana quote. 429 (More than 40 requests a minute from one address): Sent with Retry-After: 20. 502 (Solana could not be read): Try again in a minute. A signature found this way is only a lead. It still passes the same checks as one you paste, and it is the verify step that records a payment. The narrow RPC proxy the wallet payment uses is described on the Solana page.

chunks.title: Solana Pay
chunks.text: Not a Solana signature (400): A 0x hash, or text that is not base58, was given for a Solana quote. Failed on Solana, so nothing was paid (422): The transaction ran and failed. Not finalized yet (202): Seen but not final, or not yet known to the node. Check again shortly. Sent SOL to another address (422): The treasury was not a recipient. Sent a token other than USDC or USDT (422): Only the two mints above count. Not its associated account (422): The token went to another account of the treasury; write to hello@gullylabs.xyz. Already used for a payment (409): One signature pays one thing. Paid before your checkout was opened, or after its quote ran out (422): It falls outside the quote’s life. Solana could not be read just now (502): Every RPC failed; try again in a minute.

chunks.title: Solana Pay
chunks.text: Solana checkout is on only while the owner has set the Solana treasury wallet. Unset, Solana assets are not offered, and a quote on Solana is refused with “Payments on Solana cannot be taken yet”. There is never a fallback address.

chunks.title: Chain Kit
chunks.text: A new chain needs a block explorer on day one. Chain Kit is Blockscout, the open-source explorer, set up for your chain, in your brand, and run for you by Gully Labs. Chain Kit: a branded Blockscout block explorer for your EVM chain, deployed and operated by Gully Labs. What is included, how to request one from the app, and its status.

chunks.title: Chain Kit
chunks.text: Chain Kit is a managed deployment of Blockscout for one EVM chain. We size the server and the RPC for your chain, deploy the indexer and the explorer on a domain you choose, apply your branding through configuration rather than a fork, and keep it indexed, upgraded and backed up. It is available on request today. The product page is gullylabs.xyz/chain-kit.

chunks.title: Chain Kit
chunks.text: Full explorer (Blockscout): Blocks, transactions, addresses, tokens, NFTs, contract verification, APIs and charts Your brand (configuration): Your name, logos, colours and links across the explorer, so upgrades stay simple Rollups (profiles): Arbitrum Nitro and Orbit chains like Robinhood Chain, and chains with a stablecoin as gas Operations (run for you): Provisioning, TLS, backups, upgrades and monitoring, with a runbook for common failures Sizing (before any promise): A busy rollup needs terabytes; a young chain far less. We size it to your chain first

chunks.title: Chain Kit
chunks.text: Sign in to the app at app.gullylabs.xyz and open Chain Kit under Services. Give an email to reach you and your chain: its name, chain id and an RPC. Then press “Request your explorer”. The card shows “requested” with the date for your workspace. We reply by email with questions about history, settlement layer and sizing. You can also write to us from the contact form at gullylabs.xyz/services (topic: Infrastructure).

chunks.title: Chain Kit
chunks.text: Chain Kit explorers run on their own servers, so they are not part of this API yet and publish no figures here: the chart below says so rather than drawing made-up numbers. What is live is the Gully Labs API the request goes through, checked every minute by our status checks.

chunks.title: Chain Kit
chunks.text: Blockscout is GPL-3.0, and our deployment layer is GPL-3.0 too: everything we add is public at gully-labs/blockscout. You are never locked in. The product page’s “charts on day one” are illustrations badged as example data. This page charts only what our API actually reports.

chunks.title: Status
chunks.text: Every minute our server checks each part of the stack it can see from inside and keeps 24 hours of results. The public page is gullylabs.xyz/status; the same data is a JSON endpoint. The Gully Labs status page and GET /api/status: what each check means, how 24-hour uptime is computed, how incidents open and close, and the JSON shape.

chunks.title: Status
chunks.text: gullylabs.xyz/status shows the overall state, every component with its state now, a plain sentence on what was seen, its 24-hour uptime and a bar per 30 minutes, then the recent incidents. Every check is real and read-only, and the response never contains a URL, token, key or setting name: errors are reduced to plain words.

chunks.title: Status
chunks.text: Checks run every 60 seconds on the server. Public API (platform): This server is answering. The detail says how long it has been up Tracker: Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain, Solana (tracker): The chain’s token prices were read on chain in the last 10 minutes (the newest price reading, not the hourly pool discovery). 10 to 30 minutes old is degraded; older, or no price read at all, is down DeepCore launch poller (deepcore): The last good poll is within three poll intervals; within ten is degraded Telegram bot webhook (telegram): Telegram’s getWebhookInfo shows a webhook registered. A delivery error in the last 10 minutes, or more than 100 updates waiting, is degraded. See the Telegram bot page Telegram bot: News channel gate (telegram): Telegram’s getChatMember shows the bot is an admin of the News channel. If it is not, the gate cannot check membership and lets everyone through: degraded Gully Pay RPC, per payment chain (payments): A node answers eth_blockNumber (Solana: getSlot). Slower than 4 s is degraded Gully Pay fee proxies (payments): The treasury is not a fee proxy contract (if it is, checkout is refused: down), and no payment sits on a fee proxy waiting for recovery (degraded) Gully AI (ai): Configured, with a non-empty search index, and the AI provider answering for our account (a billing or key problem is degraded until an answer succeeds again)

chunks.title: Status
chunks.text: (degraded) Gully AI (ai): Configured, with a non-empty search index, and the AI provider answering for our account (a billing or key problem is degraded until an answer succeeds again) Security scan engine (security): The AI scan is configured. The detail says whether the static-analysis tools are running and what is queued Contract monitors (security): Watched contracts are read without errors; a chain failing in the last 10 minutes is degraded Holder Map sources, per chain (holders): The chain has a holder data source configured on this server off means the part is not configured on this server (for example the bot without its token): it is shown, but it is not an outage. unknown means the check could not tell, for example before the first read after a restart. “Security scan engine: up” means the AI scan can run. It is not an audit, and a clean scan is not a guarantee. See Gully Security.

chunks.title: Status
chunks.text: Each check is one sample: up counts 1, degraded counts ½, down counts 0. off and unknown samples are left out entirely, so a part that is not configured neither helps nor hurts the figure. uptime24h is the counted samples of the last 24 hours averaged, from 0 to 1. With none counted it is null, shown as “not tracked yet”, never as 0% or 100%. Each 30-minute bucket in history uses the same rule for up, and ms is the mean latency of its checks that were timed. Samples are kept for 24 hours and saved in the server’s data volume, so a restart or a deploy keeps the history. since says when it starts. overall is major when the Public API is down or three or more components are down, degraded when anything is down or degraded, and operational otherwise.

chunks.title: Status
chunks.text: An incident opens when a component goes down or degraded. While it is open its detail follows the latest check, and it is marked down if it got worse. It closes (its endedAt is set) when the component is up again, or switched off on this server. Incidents are recorded automatically from the checks, newest first; the body carries the latest 20.

Today the spec is written and a light devnet is prepared; no chain is running.

chunks.title: Roadmap
chunks.text: Gully Labs does not audit anything today and has published no audit reports. Live now: the AI Security Scan (an AI review only until our static-tools worker runs, and labelled so on every report), the Gully Score and contract monitors. A human Security Review is quoted on request. Audits open only when the people, the process and the public record behind them exist, and the changelog will say when they do. Security work on both halves of a Web3 product: the smart contracts, and the code around them. Contract audits cover Solidity on the EVM chains we already work with. Code audits cover what usually goes wrong next to the contracts: dApp frontends, backends and APIs, key management, wallet-connect and signing flows, infrastructure and CI. It follows what the established security firms offer (audits, public reports, a public project score and onchain monitoring), and the rules below are written against what their critics point out: scores whose weights are not published, badges that read as endorsements, and reports that do not say which code they covered.

chunks.title: Roadmap
chunks.text: AI Security Scan A self-serve scan of a deployed contract, a Solidity repository, an upload or a web2 codebase. Today it is an AI review only: the static-tools worker (Slither and Aderyn) is not running on our server yet, so no static analysis or fuzzing runs, and every report is labelled “AI review only — static tools unavailable” with those tools listed as not run. Once the worker runs, its tools feed the AI pass and the label changes. Free scans each month by plan, then paid with Gully Pay. The result is labelled an automated scan, never a review or an audit. Start one on gullylabs.xyz/security. Security Review People on our team read the code in scope with the scan’s output as a starting point, check each finding by hand and write up what they find. Quoted per project: ask through the form on gullylabs.xyz/security. The aim, as the practice grows, is two reviewers per review, every fix reviewed, and a report published with the client’s consent, pinned to the exact commit hash that was reviewed. Smart-contract audits and code audits Smart-contract audit: a security review plus formal checks of the core maths and accounting, a full fix review and a public report. We will use the word audit for our own work only once there is a public record of reviews and contest results to point to.

chunks.title: Roadmap
chunks.text: review and a public report. We will use the word audit for our own work only once there is a public record of reviews and contest results to point to. Code audit for the non-contract parts: dApp frontends, backends and APIs, key and secret management, wallet-connect and signing flows, infrastructure and CI, checked against a checklist based on the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS). Gully Score and monitoring Gully Score (live at gullylabs.xyz/score): a 0 to 100 score for any contract from public evidence, with every component, weight and source shown. The rules are below; the method is on Gully Score. Monitoring (live in the app): alerts when a watched contract changes its admin key, transfers ownership, moves a large amount out, pauses or upgrades, delivered by Telegram and signed webhooks, the way gap alerts are. Bug bounty hosting Later: hosting bug bounty programmes for projects we have reviewed.

chunks.title: Roadmap
chunks.text: Written before the first score was given, so they cannot be bent later. Every component, its weight and its data source is shown on the page, and the method is published with a changelog. No hidden formula. No pay-to-rank. Paying Gully Labs for anything never changes a score or a position. If a scored project is also a client, its page says so. Audit status is only ever a link to a public report, with the auditor, the date, the commit hash and the contracts in scope. If the deployed code differs from that commit, the page says so. Admin powers (minting, upgrades, pausing, privileged withdrawals) count as risks, not as out of scope. A value we cannot read shows as unreadable, never as a pass and never as zero. After an incident the earlier score stays visible, marked, next to what happened. A score is information, not an endorsement and not investment advice. Identity checks, if we ever do them, are shown as identity only, never as a safety signal. The weights below are read live from the public API in your browser, so this page and the score agree.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: An Arbitrum (Orbit) chain run by Gully Labs, with Chain Kit as its explorer, Gully Pay native on it, and Hyperlane as its interop layer once it launches. This page summarises the spec for developers and says exactly what exists today. The plan for the Gully L3: an Arbitrum chain settling to Arbitrum One with Chain Kit, Gully Pay and Hyperlane as its interop layer. Status: spec written, devnet prepared, nothing running.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: Spec written. Devnet prepared. Nothing is running. There is no public RPC, no explorer, no faucet, no bridge and no Hyperlane deployment yet. The light devnet (one Arbitrum Nitro node in dev mode, chain id 412346) and the Hyperlane validator and relayer are prepared as compose files that refuse to start without free disk and RAM. The changelog will say when any of this goes live; until then, the waitlist in the app dashboard is the only thing you can join. S0 · light devnet (Nitro --dev, chain id 412346, in-memory parent): Prepared, not started. Local testing of Chain Kit, Stylus, Gully Pay and the Hyperlane agents. S1 · Gully Devnet (A public Arbitrum chain on Arbitrum Sepolia): Planned. Public RPC, Chain Kit explorer, faucet, canonical bridge, Hyperlane to Arbitrum Sepolia. S2 · Gully L3 (Production, settling to Arbitrum One (recommended)): Planned. Gully venues, Gully Pay, Warp Routes for USDC and ETH, aggregator listings. The Gully L3 is one track of the Roadmap, next to Gully Security.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: An Arbitrum chain (the stack formerly branded Orbit): Nitro, deployed with the Arbitrum chain SDK through the parent chain’s RollupCreator and TokenBridgeCreator, with the Gully stack attached on day one. Explorer: Chain Kit, our Blockscout fork, with its Arbitrum profile (CHAIN_TYPE=arbitrum, traces from the node’s debug API). Payments: Gully Pay native on the chain, with USDC and ETH as assets, verified on chain the way it is today. Interop: Hyperlane. A Mailbox on the L3, Warp Routes for USDC and ETH from Arbitrum One (and Base) into it, and our own validator and relayer. Analytics, alerts, Gully AI read it like any other chain. The chain id for the public chains is not chosen yet: 412346 is the fixed id of the dev node and will not be reused for a public chain. It will be registered in ethereum-lists/chains and the Hyperlane registry before the devnet opens.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: Both Arbitrum One and Base have canonical RollupCreator factories, so either can be the parent. The spec recommends Arbitrum One: the tooling we forked, the Chain Kit profile, the tracker’s Robinhood Chain coverage and the Arbitrum ecosystem programs are all Arbitrum-shaped, and Base liquidity still reaches the L3 through a Base→L3 Warp Route and, later, the aggregators. The public devnet settles to Arbitrum Sepolia. The parent’s gas price is one input to what posting a batch costs. These are the base fees on the candidates right now, read from their public RPCs by our server; a chain that cannot be read says so. The other input, the parent’s own L1 data component, varies with Ethereum blob prices and is not reported by any public RPC, so the spec asks for a real batch to be measured on each testnet before the decision is final.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: Rollup (recommended) (Batches are posted to the parent chain as calldata or blobs. No extra infrastructure.): Security is the parent’s. Costs track the parent’s gas; for an L3 the parent is an L2, so already cheap. AnyTrust (A Data Availability Committee you run (one DA server per member) signs certificates; the batch poster posts the certificate. Falls back to posting full data if signatures do not arrive.): Lower DA fees, but N machines around the clock, and a committee run by one operator removes no trust. The devnet and the launch use Rollup mode. AnyTrust is reconsidered only if the batch poster’s measured spend on Arbitrum Sepolia, projected to production volume, exceeds the cost of a real committee.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: ETH. A custom ERC-20 gas token is possible (18 decimals, no transfer fee, no rebasing, no transfer callbacks, already on the parent chain) but in Rollup mode it needs a fee token pricer contract supplying the ETH/token rate to reimburse the batch poster, and every wallet, bridge and aggregator must learn the token. Gully has no token, and the spec does not propose one.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: Hyperlane is the interop layer for the Gully L3 when it launches, not before. LI.FI and Relay stay the swap and bridge aggregators for the chains Gully Pay offers today. What gets deployed on the L3 Mailbox (Dispatches and processes messages): One per chain, deployed with hyperlane core deploy. Default ISM (Verifies inbound messages): Devnet: a trusted-relayer ISM (testing). Public chain: a multisig ISM per origin; for messages from Arbitrum, the public Arbitrum validator set already in the registry. Merkle tree hook (Inserts each message into the tree validators sign): Default hook. Interchain gas paymaster (Senders pay the relayer in the origin chain’s gas): Gas oracle entries for Arbitrum One (and Base) kept current by us. Validator announce (Validators publish where their signatures live): One per chain. Nothing is deployed on Arbitrum One, Base or Arbitrum Sepolia: their Mailboxes already exist (addresses in the Hyperlane registry). Warp Routes A USDC route locks native USDC on Arbitrum One (collateral) and mints a synthetic USDC on the L3; Base can be added as a second collateral chain. An ETH route is the fast path beside the canonical bridge, whose withdrawals wait the parent’s challenge window. Route contracts are owned by the team multisig, never a server key. Security Review. Engineers on our team read your code with the scan’s output as a starting point, check the findings by hand, look at the logic the tools cannot follow, and write up what they find. What you get: A scope agreed with you before work starts; Findings checked by a person, with fixes discussed; A written report. Limits: Quoted after we see the code; no list price; A time-boxed review, not a guarantee. Audit. A full audit is planned as a later tier. We do not sell it today and it cannot be requested yet. chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: We collect as little as we can to run what you use, we don’t sell it, and we don’t use it for advertising. This page says what we collect, why, who else sees it and how long we keep it, product by product. It covers gullylabs.xyz, docs.gullylabs.xyz, the Gully Labs app at app.gullylabs.xyz, blog.gullylabs.xyz, analytics.gullylabs.xyz, the payment pages, Gully AI, and the @GullyLabsBot Telegram bot and its Mini App.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Gully Labs (“we”, “us”) builds and runs these sites and services. We decide what personal data they collect and why, so we are responsible for it. If you run a Gully Pay store or use Gully Analytics on your own site, you are responsible for your own customers’ and visitors’ data, and we process it for you to provide the service. Questions or requests about your data: hello@gullylabs.xyz.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Signing in with your wallet. The app signs you in with Sign-In with Ethereum: you sign a message, and no password or email is needed. We keep your wallet address, when you first and last signed in, and whether the account is blocked. Each sign-in creates a session that stores a hash of a random session id (never the id itself), when it was created, last used and expires, your browser’s user agent and which workspace you have open. We don’t store your IP address with your account or sessions. Workspaces and teams. A workspace’s name, its members’ wallet addresses and roles, who invited whom and when, and invites (an invite link is kept only as a hash). If you add them: a display name, an email address, notification choices, and company details (name, postal address, tax ID) for invoices. To show your ENS or Basename we look your address up through public Ethereum and Base nodes and keep the answer for 24 hours. An activity log records who changed what in the workspace (for example a key created or a plan paid), without IP addresses. API keys and usage. We keep a hash of each key (never the key itself), its prefix and name, and count requests per key: per hour by result and endpoint, per day, and the last 50 requests (time, method, path, status and response time). Anonymous requests are limited per IP address in memory only; we don’t store those IPs. Contact and waitlists. When you write to us through the contact form: your name, email, message, the kind of project and budget you pick. When you join a waitlist: your email and which list.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Gully Analytics is our own, self-hosted fork of the open-source Umami analytics, at analytics.gullylabs.xyz. We use it on our own sites, and customers can use it on theirs. It sets no cookies. A visit is grouped by a hash of the site, your IP address, your browser and a salt that changes every month, so we can’t follow you from month to month. Your IP address is used to work out your country, region and city and is then dropped; it isn’t stored. We also record the page, referrer, browser, operating system, device type, screen size and language. On pages where you connect a wallet (the app and payment pages), it records wallet connects and disconnects, chain switches and transactions you send, with the chain and wallet type. By default the wallet address is stored only as a short hash (the first 16 characters of its SHA-256). That is pseudonymous, not anonymous: anyone who knows your address can compute the same hash. To opt out in a browser, set the local storage value umami.disabled to 1 for the site. If you sign up for Gully Analytics, we also keep your wallet address, your sites, your plan and trial dates, and monthly event counts. Your Umami password is never stored by us.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: When you ask Gully AI a question (on the site, in the app or with /ask in Telegram), we log the question, how long the answer was (not the answer itself), which sources and live tools it used, whether you were signed in, and a salted hash of your IP address, or of your Telegram chat id. If you rate an answer with a thumbs up or down, we keep the rating with the question and the same hash, so we know which docs to write. We keep questions and ratings for 90 days. To write the answer, the question, your last few messages in that conversation and the matching passages of our docs are sent to Anthropic (Claude). When semantic search is switched on, the question is also sent to Voyage AI to compare it with our docs. When you are signed in to the app (or ask in a private Telegram chat linked to your wallet), Gully AI can read your own workspace’s store, API usage and alerts to answer, read-only; it never sees another workspace. The app also remembers your recent questions in your own browser.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Using @GullyLabsBot requires following the Gully Labs News channel; the bot checks this with Telegram and remembers the answer for up to 30 minutes, in memory only. If you link a chat to your wallet for alerts, we keep the chat id and type, the chat’s title (for a private chat, your first and last name and @username as Telegram gives them), your Telegram user id and when you linked it. Link codes are kept only as hashes and expire after 10 minutes. You can unlink at any time with /stop or in the bot’s settings. Bot records. For every chat that uses the bot we keep when it was first and last seen, its language, whether it is linked to a wallet, whether it follows the News channel, whether it has blocked the bot or switched announcements off, and how it found the bot. No names and no message text are kept in these records.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: the News channel, whether it has blocked the bot or switched announcements off, and how it found the bot. No names and no message text are kept in these records. Announcements. The bot sometimes sends news to chats chosen by those records (for example, linked chats, chats with alerts, followers of the News channel, a language, or chats active recently). For each announcement we keep, per recipient chat, whether it was delivered (with Telegram’s message id or error). Its buttons go through a link made for that recipient, so when you open one we record that this recipient opened it, once; we don’t record when, your IP address or your browser. Our operators see delivery and opens with chat ids shortened to their last 4 digits. Every announcement has a 🔕 Stop announcements button, and Settings switches them off and on again; that never affects your alerts. The Mini App checks Telegram’s signed launch data to know who you are and stores nothing: no cookie and no session.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Scans. When your workspace runs an AI Security Scan we keep a record of it: the workspace, the wallet that started it, when, what was scanned (a contract address and chain, a GitHub repository and commit, or an uploaded file’s name and size), its price or invoice and its status. To run the scan we store the code on our server: the file you upload, the full text of the source files fetched from the chain’s explorer or GitHub or unpacked from your upload, the tools’ output, the AI’s findings and the report. For a web2 scan, files named.env are stored with the rest of the code but are never sent to the AI or the scanning tools. Please don’t upload secrets. Who sees it. Members of your workspace see its scans and reports; developers, admins and owners can start and cancel them. Gully Labs operators can see the list of scans (who started one, the target and its status). To review the code, the files in scope are sent to Anthropic (Claude) after common secret patterns (API keys, private-key blocks and similar) are replaced; that check works by pattern and can miss a secret. When our static-tools worker runs (it does not yet), it receives the code too, on our own servers. The contract address and chain are sent to Etherscan, Blockscout or Sourcify to fetch verified source, the repository and commit to GitHub, and for web2 scans the dependency list in package-lock.json to the npm registry.

chunks.text: are sent to Etherscan, Blockscout or Sourcify to fetch verified source, the repository and commit to GitHub, and for web2 scans the dependency list in package-lock.json to the npm registry. Publishing. A workspace owner or admin can publish a finished report. It then becomes public: the target, the findings, file paths with their hashes, and any code comments the scan flagged as attempts to instruct the AI; draft proof-of-concept code and the workspace are left out. Search engines are asked not to index it unless the publisher allows it. Published reports count towards that contract’s Gully Score. Unpublishing takes the report off the site at once; the copy stays on our server, not shown. Security Review requests. When you ask for a quote we keep what you send (name, email, project, scope, repository, contract, company, timeline) and the signed-in wallet if there is one. The request also goes to our enquiries inbox and to our operators’ Telegram chat. Requests are limited per IP address and email in memory only; the IP is not stored.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: The request also goes to our enquiries inbox and to our operators’ Telegram chat. Requests are limited per IP address and email in memory only; the IP is not stored. Monitors. For each contract your workspace watches we keep the contract, chain and name, your alert thresholds, your webhook address and its signing secret, whether Telegram is on, whether the contract may be listed publicly, the contract’s last read state, its last 100 events and the last 50 alert deliveries. The contract is read through public blockchain nodes. Events a monitor sees are public chain data. A monitor whose listing is on adds them to that contract’s public Gully Score. With listing off, nothing the monitor records reaches the public: not the contract’s score, the public list of scores, the sitemap, score badges or Gully AI; a score already worked out from it is dropped and worked out again without it.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Holder Map. Looking up a map needs no account. To show the maps opened most today we count one view per visitor per token per day, using a hash of the IP address made with a random key that is held in memory only and replaced every day; the counts are reset each UTC day. New maps are limited per IP address for a minute, in memory only. To build a map we send the token’s address (never anything about you) to DeepCore, Blockscout, Moralis, Solana nodes and public blockchain nodes. Holder alerts are kept like other alerts, until you delete them. Gully Score. Looking up a score needs no account and we don’t record who looked. We keep each contract’s latest score and its history. The contract address is sent to Sourcify, Etherscan and public blockchain nodes to read its evidence. Lookups are limited per IP address in memory only.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Payments happen on public blockchains. A transaction, the addresses in it and the amount are public and permanent, and nobody (us included) can change or delete them. We never hold your funds. When you pay us or a Gully Pay store, we record the transaction hash, chain, asset, amount, its US dollar value at the time, the paying address and the block, to confirm and receipt the payment. A store’s owner sees its own payments, and its webhook sends the payment, including the paying address, to the address the store sets. A store can put a customer name and email on an invoice; the store decides that, and is responsible for it. We count how often an invoice page is opened, without storing who opened it. For a store we keep its name, logo (copied once from the address given, never hot-linked), accent colour, support email, website, receiving wallets, which version of the merchant terms it accepted and with which wallet, its invoices, links, fees and statements.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: One cookie of ours: the app’s sign-in cookie (__Host-gl_dev), only after you sign in. It is HttpOnly, sent only to the app over HTTPS, and lasts 30 days or until you sign out. No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies, and Gully Analytics uses none. Browser storage remembers choices on your device only: the app’s sidebar, invites you declined, that you accepted the swap risk notice, recent Gully AI questions in the app, and requests you already sent (Chain Kit, devnet waitlist). The blog (Ghost) runs on our server and handles its own visitors; its member sign-up is switched off.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: We don’t sell personal data or share it for advertising. These services see some of it because they carry or power what you use: Cloudflare carries all traffic to our sites, so it sees your IP address and requests, and tells our server your country. Its Web Analytics beacon runs on our pages. Anthropic and, when switched on, Voyage AI: Gully AI questions, as above. Anthropic also reviews the code of Gully Security scans. Etherscan, Blockscout, Sourcify, GitHub and the npm registry: the contract, repository or dependency list a Gully Security scan or a Gully Score reads, as above. DeepCore, Blockscout and Moralis: token addresses for the Holder Map, as above. Telegram: everything you send to or receive from the bot. Blockchain node providers (public RPC endpoints): we read transactions, balances and ENS names through them, which can include your address. Your wallet talks to its own nodes. Wallet and swap services you choose to use: WalletConnect when you connect a wallet that way, LI.FI in the swap widget, and Jupiter for Solana swaps (it receives your public key). Addresses you give us: alert and store webhooks are sent to the URLs you set. We may disclose data when the law requires it, to protect our users or services from fraud or abuse, or to a buyer if Gully Labs is sold, under this policy.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Sessions last 30 days. Gully AI questions and ratings are kept 90 days. The activity log keeps 180 days, and so does a security scan’s code. Backups are kept 7 days. Accounts, payments and stores are not deleted automatically today. Sign-in sessions: 30 days from sign-in (at most 20 per wallet), or until you sign out or revoke them. Team invites: 7 days to accept; closed invites are deleted 30 days after they close. Workspace activity log: The newest 1,000 events, none older than 180 days. API usage counts per key: Hourly counts 31 days; the last 50 requests and daily totals until the key or account is deleted. Gully AI questions and ratings: 90 days. Telegram link codes: 10 minutes to use; deleted a day after they expire. Unpaid payment quotes: Deleted 7 days after they expire. Webhook deliveries: The newest 1,000 for Gully Pay; the newest 50 per gap alert. Contact form messages: The newest 5,000 messages. Security scans: the code, the fetched sources, tool output and the report: Deleted within a day of the scan being finished and 180 days old (a daily clean-up); the scan’s entry in your list (without the code) is not deleted automatically. Code uploaded for a scan: Moved into the scan when it starts; deleted at once if a free scan cannot start or you cancel an unpaid scan; a paid scan left unpaid for 24 hours has its uploaded code deleted and its invoice cancelled.
