chunks.text: once if a free scan cannot start or you cancel an unpaid scan; a paid scan left unpaid for 24 hours has its uploaded code deleted and its invoice cancelled. Published scan reports: Public until unpublished; after that the copy stays on our server, not shown, and is not deleted automatically. Security Review requests: The newest 5,000 requests. Security monitors: Until you delete the monitor; each keeps its last 100 events and last 50 alert deliveries. Gully Score results and history: Not deleted automatically (who looked a score up is not recorded). Holder Map view counts: Reset every UTC day; the key that hashes visitors is never written down. Telegram announcements: deliveries and opened links: The newest 200 announcements. Telegram bot records (first and last seen, language, opt-out): Not deleted automatically today. Backups of all of the above: 7 days. Accounts, workspaces, keys, payments, invoices, stores, Telegram links, waitlists, analytics data: Not deleted automatically today; ask us and we delete what the law lets us.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: We store hashes instead of secrets wherever we can (session ids, API keys, invite and link codes, IP addresses in the Gully AI log and the Holder Map counts), use HTTPS everywhere, and back the data up every night to the same server, keeping 7 days. No system is perfectly secure; if a breach affects your data, we will tell you as the law requires.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Sign out, or revoke any session, in the app’s Settings. Revoke API keys, delete alerts, remove webhooks and switch off pay links in the app. Unlink Telegram with /stop or in the bot’s settings, and switch announcements off with 🔕 Stop announcements or in Settings. Delete a monitor, or unpublish a scan report, in the app; ask us to delete a scan’s code before the 180 days are up. Opt out of Gully Analytics as described above, or use a browser that blocks scripts. Ask us at hello@gullylabs.xyz to see, correct, export or delete what we hold about you off-chain. The app doesn’t have a self-service “delete my account” button yet, so email us and we will do it. We may keep payment records where the law requires, and we can’t delete anything that is on a public blockchain. Depending on where you live, you may also have the right to object to or restrict how we use your data, and to complain to your data protection authority. Our services are not meant for anyone under 18.

chunks.title: Privacy policy

chunks.title: Gully Pay fee split: which contract and why
chunks.section: Gully Pay fee split: which existing contract
chunks.text: *Question. Which existing contract, already deployed, can pay the merchant and send the Gully Labs fee to the treasury in one transaction, without custody? *Answer. Use Request Network's ERC20FeeProxy for tokens (USDC and USDT) on Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain and Arbitrum, and since 2026-10-18 on OP Mainnet too, whose proxy is byte-identical to Base's (section "Chains added 2026-10-18" below). Keep native coin (ETH, BNB, POL, AVAX), Polygon, Avalanche and Robinhood Chain on plain transfers, with the fee invoiced as it is today. Gully Labs deploys nothing, and the custom splitter on this branch has been deleted. Checked on 2026-10-17. Every address was read with eth_getCode through the same public RPCs that server/payments.mjs uses.

chunks.title: Gully Pay fee split: which contract and why

chunks.title: Roadmap: the Gully L3 spec
chunks.text: From the Arbitrum docs (choose AnyTrust and Inside AnyTrust, read 2026-10-17): Rollup: "Transaction data is posted to the parent chain as calldata or blobs", DataAvailabilityCommittee: false, "No additional steps are required." Security is the parent's. AnyTrust: a Data Availability Committee "which is a group of permissioned nodes that you choose and run, or outsource to a Rollup-as-a-Service (RaaS)". The batch poster posts a DACert "signed by the required number of DAC members (configurable)"; with N members the certificate needs N-1 signatures and the assumption is that "at least two are honest". If the sequencer cannot collect enough signatures "within a few minutes" it posts the full data to the parent chain instead (rollup fallback). Setup: "Deploy a Data Availability Server (DAS) for each DAC member", generate a BLS keyset, register it on SequencerInbox. Costs: The Arbitrum docs give no figure for either mode; they say the parent-chain data posting is "the largest component of the cost of using Arbitrum". For an L3 the parent is itself an L2, whose calldata is already cheap (base fees of 0.005 to 0.02 gwei measured above, plus the L2's own L1 data component). AnyTrust adds machines: one DAS per committee member, around the clock, plus mirrors. A committee run entirely by us has N members but one operator, so it removes no trust; it only cuts DA fees. *Recommendation: Rollup (D2) for S1 and the launch. Measure the batch poster's monthly spend on Arbitrum Sepolia during S1; switch to AnyTrust only if that spend, projected to S2 volume, exceeds the cost of running a real committee (at least four DAS machines plus a second operator).

chunks.title: Roadmap: the Gully L3 spec
chunks.text: Options and their rules (Arbitrum docs, choose a custom gas token and the custom gas token on AnyTrust page, 2026-10-17): ETH (default): nothing to configure; wallets, LI.FI, Relay and Hyperlane's gas oracles all understand it; Gully Pay already prices ETH with the same-chain Chainlink feed. Custom ERC-20: "Must be a standard ERC-20 token", "Must not be rebasing or include transfer fees", transfers and approvals "must occur directly via the token contract, not via proxies or hooks", no transfer callbacks; 18 decimals (SDK guides). It must already exist on the parent chain and is "natively bridged" at deployment. In Rollup mode the batch poster is reimbursed in the fee token, so a fee token pricer contract supplying the ETH/token exchange rate must be deployed and registered on the parent; the docs' three examples are marked as not for production and "If the fee token pricer returns stale or manipulated prices, the batch poster may be under- or over-reimbursed." On AnyTrust the chain owner must also call SetL1PricePerUnit(0) and SetL1PricingRewardRate(0) or "Nitro will apply a parent chain's fee to all transactions". *Recommendation: ETH (D3). Gully has no token; a gas token would be a new product with its own risks (the pricer, liquidity, listings). If the owner wants a Gully gas token later, it is a new chain parameter at deployment time, not a switch.

chunks.title: Treasury Safe: how the Gully Labs treasury Safe is deployed
chunks.section: The treasury Safe on every chain (one-click deployment)
chunks.text: Gully Pay pays GULLY_TREASURY_ADDRESS on every chain it offers. When that address is a Safe, it exists only on the chains where the Safe was deployed: elsewhere it is an empty address, and a payment sent there is lost. The admin panel's Treasury Safe card (/admin, under Subscriptions) reads the treasury on every chain and offers Deploy Safe on where it has no code. Your own wallet signs; the server never holds a key. Server: server/safe-deploy.mjs. Browser: src/components/pay/SafeDeploy.tsx, src/pages/admin/TreasurySafe.tsx. Tests: npm run test:safe-deploy (stubbed chains, real Safe 1.4.1 bytes) and the live Base Sepolia run in contracts/TESTNET-RESULTS.md, section "Safe deployment".

chunks.title: Treasury Safe: how the Gully Labs treasury Safe is deployed
chunks.text: Pill — Meaning Safe 1.4.1 · 1/2 — A Safe we recognise (1.3.0 or 1.4.1 from Safe's official factory): version, threshold / owners. Payments there are fine. not deployed — No code at the treasury address on this chain. Payments there would be lost. The Deploy button appears when the Safe exists on another chain. wallet (EIP-7702) — The treasury is a delegated EOA there; it receives as a wallet. contract, not a Safe — Code we do not recognise as a Safe proxy. Nothing is offered; look at it by hand. unreadable — Every RPC for that chain failed. Try again; see GULLY_RPC_. ahead of payments — OP Mainnet, Polygon and Avalanche are listed before Gully Pay takes payments there, so the Safe can be in place first. Once feat/pay-chains lists a chain in server/payments.mjs, that entry wins and the pill goes. If the treasury is a normal wallet (no code anywhere), the card says so: nothing to deploy.

chunks.title: Treasury Safe: how the Gully Labs treasury Safe is deployed
chunks.section: Deploying the treasury Safe on OP Mainnet, Polygon or Avalanche (owner steps)
chunks.text: Open /admin with the admin token. In Treasury Safe, the Base row should read Safe 1.4.1 · … (the origin) and the target row not deployed. Press Deploy Safe on OP Mainnet (or Polygon, Avalanche). The panel reads the Safe on Base, recovers its creation transaction, checks that Safe's official factory, singleton and fallback handler are on the target chain with the pinned code hashes, and shows: the Safe address with address verified (the server's and the page's own CREATE2 arithmetic agree), the owners it will start with, the gas estimate in the chain's coin, and every check. Read the warnings: the copy starts with the Safe's ORIGINAL owners and threshold (the ones in its creation transaction). If owners were changed since, change them again on the new chain afterwards, from Safe{Wallet}. Press Connect a wallet to deploy and connect any wallet that holds a little of the chain's coin for gas (about 240,000 gas; the panel shows the cost). It does not have to be a Safe owner. The wallet is asked to switch to the chain (and to add it, if it is new to the wallet), then to confirm one transaction to Safe's factory 0x4e1D…ec67 (1.4.1) or 0xa6B7…6AB2 (1.3.0). The stepper runs Sent → Mined → Verified on chain: the server reads the receipt, then eth_getCode and getOwners() at the treasury address. On Verified the card re-reads the chains and the row turns green. Only then let that chain take payments (feat/pay-chains): the same check that refuses a merchant's undeployed Safe refuses our own treasury per chain, and it passes once the code is there. Repeat per chain. The same Safe address appears on every chain; nothing about Base changes.

chunks.title: Treasury Safe: how the Gully Labs treasury Safe is deployed
chunks.text: A prediction that differs from the Safe's address (mismatch): nothing is offered. Both the server and the browser recompute CREATE2 before the wallet is asked. No official factory/singleton/fallback handler on the target chain, or code there whose keccak differs from the pinned hash (no-factory, no-fallback). A Safe created with createProxy (plain CREATE, 1.3.0) or by a factory we do not know: its address cannot be reproduced. Create a new Safe for that chain instead and change GULLY_TREASURY_ADDRESS… per chain is not supported (one address everywhere), so for the treasury this means a new Safe everywhere. A setup that paid for its own deployment (paymentToken/payment), or whose module set-up call targets a contract missing on the target chain. The fee-proxy addresses (server/fee-proxy-guard.mjs) and the zero address are never a target.

chunks.title: Treasury Safe: how the Gully Labs treasury Safe is deployed
chunks.text: The salt nonce and the exact initializer are not stored on chain. The server looks, in order: our own record (DATA_DIR/safe-deploys.json, Safes planned as new here), a transaction hash you paste (deployTx), the first block in which the Safe had code (binary search over eth_getCode, needs a node with archive state: drpc and Base's own RPCs have it; publicnode does not without a key) and that block's ProxyCreation log, then Safe's transaction service as a hint. Every path is verified by recomputing the address; a wrong hash is simply refused. If the panel says the creation could not be found, open the treasury on the origin chain's explorer, copy the "Contract Creator" transaction hash and call POST /api/admin/safe/plan { chainId, deployTx } (or paste it when the panel asks, once that field is wired; today the API takes it).

chunks.title: Treasury Safe: how the Gully Labs treasury Safe is deployed
chunks.text: GULLY_RPC_ overrides the public RPCs for any chain, the extra Safe chains included (10, 137, 43114). GULLY_TESTNET_CHAINS=84532,11155420,421614 adds Base Sepolia, OP Sepolia and Arbitrum Sepolia; ignored when NODE_ENV=production. DATA_DIR/safe-deploys.json: Safes planned as new (address, owners, threshold, salt nonce, initializer, per-chain deployment tx). It is what makes a second deployment of the same new Safe instant. Backed up with the data volume. Pinned deployments: safe-global/safe-deployments 1.37.64 (addresses and code hashes in server/safe-deploy.mjs). A new Safe version means adding its factory, singletons and handler there, with their hashes, nothing else.

chunks.title: Launchpad integration: Holder Map on launchpads
chunks.text: A public HTTPS endpoint that answers "is this address one of your launches?" for a chain and token: A URL we can fill in with the chain id and the lowercase token address, for example https://api.yourpad.example/v1/tokens/{chainId}/{token} (or one host per chain). 404 when the token is not yours. 200 with JSON otherwise. In the JSON: the chain id, the token address, and the creator address. Ideally also the creation block number; if you do not publish it we find the block ourselves on an archive node. If your API also returns non-launch tokens (for example tracked or listed tokens), a field that tells launches apart (we match one field to one value, such as kind == "LAUNCH"). Optional: an endpoint that gives the main pool address of a token. Reasonable limits: we call it at most 120 times a minute in total, 6 second timeout, results cached for a day.

chunks.title: Launchpad integration: Holder Map on launchpads
chunks.text: Per chain, the address of the factory (or hook) contract that emits an event when a token is created. The event signature, for example TokenCreated(address,address,uint256). Where the token address sits in it (which indexed topic, 1 to 3) and where the creator address sits (an indexed topic, or a data word number). We never guess these. We only use addresses that come from you or from your published deployments. Both options can be combined: an API entry may also carry the factory event as a fallback for when your API is down.

chunks.title: Launchpad integration: Holder Map on launchpads
chunks.text: The embed: one tag shows the Holder Map on any page of yours. It frames https://gullylabs.xyz/embed/holders/:chain/:token, which can also be framed directly. data-chain is one of robinhood|bsc|base|hyperevm|solana; data-height is 360 to 2000 (default 760). A "Powered by Gully Labs" credit shows on the free embed. The badge: GET https://gullylabs.xyz/api/holders/:chain/:token/card.png is a 1200 x 630 share card that shows a token's holder picture; use it as an image link or as og:image. It leads to https://gullylabs.xyz/holders/:chain/:token. The API: GET https://gullylabs.xyz/api/holders/:chain/:token returns the whole map as JSON (CORS open). No key needed; a key raises the rate limit. The SDK: @gullylabs/holders (in the gully-sdk repo; not published yet) has a typed client (createHoldersClient({ baseUrl, apiKey? }) with getMap(chain, token) and cardUrl(chain, token)) and a React component that frames the embed. Recognition: once your entry is in the registry, knownLaunch(chain, token) recognises your launches by chain and token and returns the creator, creation block and pool for the Holder Map to use.

chunks.title: Launchpad integration: Holder Map on launchpads
chunks.text: The registry is the LAUNCHPADS array in server/holders-launchpads.mjs. Adding a launchpad is adding one object; validateLaunchpad() checks every entry when the module loads (a bad entry throws, so run the test first) and listLaunchpads() exposes only { id, name, url, chains } publicly. Steps: Get the details above from the partner. Never fill in an address ourselves. Add the entry to LAUNCHPADS. Check the chain ids against HOLDER_CHAINS in server/holders.mjs. Add or extend a case in scripts/test-launchpads.mjs (it has a fake entry of each lookup type to copy), then run npm run test:launchpads. Check against a real launch from the partner on the staging server (knownLaunch(chain, token) returns { venue, chainId, token, creationBlock, deployer, pool? }), then ship it with the normal deploy. chunks.section: Steps to run the code locally
chunks.text: Clone the Arbitrum token bridge repository from Github onto your local machine Use the Node version as per project settings to avoid any errors before project installation. Install dependencies in all packages using yarn. Set env vars: Copy the existing env.local.sample file present. In .env created, add NEXT_PUBLIC_INFURA_KEY=my-infura-key (Optional) If you want to use a different RPC provider or your own RPC, please see RPC Configuration. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID to your WalletConnect project ID. You can create a new project on the WalletConnect dashboard. Build the project and internal packages Finally, running the project (back in root dir:) Visit http://localhost:3000/

chunks.title: Stock token fair-price gap (Tracker)
chunks.text: Stock token fair-price gap is part of Tracker. Status: live now. Shows every tracked tokenised stock at its onchain price next to its fair price and the percentage gap between them, read live. Chains: Robinhood Chain (33 stock tokens in server/data/robinhood-stocks.json), BNB Chain (14 Binance bStocks in bsc-stocks.json) and Solana (49 xStocks in solana-stocks.json). Fair price is a Chainlink feed read on chain with latestRoundData(); on BNB Chain it is the feed times the token's uiMultiplier(); on Solana, where a share has no Chainlink feed, it is the issuer's xStocks quote. Onchain price is read from each token's deepest pool; DexScreener or GeckoTerminal only find the pool. A pool under MIN_LIQUIDITY_USD (10,000) is shown but never flagged; a gap under IN_LINE_PCT (1) is "in line"; a gap of IMPLAUSIBLE_PCT (15) or more is withheld as unverified unless the pool holds TRUST_LIQUIDITY_USD (1,000,000) or more and was read on chain. A price that cannot be read is reported as unreadable, never as zero. History snapshots are taken every 5 minutes and kept for 7 days.

chunks.title: Gap movers and gap index (Tracker)
chunks.text: Gap movers and gap index is part of Tracker. Status: live now. Lists the stock tokens whose gap has moved most over the last hour or day, and a single gap index across the tracker. Mover windows are 1h and 24h (MOVER_WINDOWS in server/movers.mjs). Endpoints: GET /api/tracker/movers and GET /api/tracker/gap-index. Movers are in percentage points of gap, with the gap then and now.

chunks.title: Stock pages (Tracker)
chunks.text: Stock pages is part of Tracker. Status: live now. Gives every tracked stock token its own page with price against fair price, the gap chart, pool depth, contracts, swap, alerts and its Holder Map. Pages live at /tracker/<chain>/<TICKER>; the chain keys are robinhood, bsc and solana. The gap chart shows 24 hours or 7 days from the tracker's five-minute snapshots, with drag-to-zoom. The page links to the app's Alerts tab with the token preset, and copies an embeddable badge. A value that could not be read shows a dash, never zero.

chunks.title: Public tracker API (Tracker)
chunks.text: Public tracker API is part of Tracker. Status: live now. A read-only JSON API for the tracker, open without a key; a key raises the rate limit. Endpoints include GET /api/tracker, /api/tracker/history, /api/tracker/movers, /api/tracker/gap-index, /api/plans, /api/status and /api/stats. Anonymous callers get ANONYMOUS.perMin (60) requests a minute per IP and 7 days of history (server/plans.mjs). Keys are Bearer tokens that start gl_live_.

chunks.title: In-page stock token swaps (Tracker)
chunks.text: In-page stock token swaps is part of Tracker. Status: live now. Lets a visitor swap into or out of a stock token from its page, routed by LI.FI on Robinhood Chain and BNB Chain and by Jupiter on Solana. The visitor's own wallet signs everything. Solana quotes and swap transactions go through GET /api/solana/jupiter/quote and POST /api/solana/jupiter/swap; the server returns an unsigned transaction and holds no key. A region check (GET /api/geo, from Cloudflare's CF-IPCountry header) can close the swap card; the list is in server/geo.mjs.

chunks.title: Solana xStocks coverage (Tracker)
chunks.text: Solana xStocks coverage is part of Tracker. Status: live now. Extends the tracker to Solana xStocks, with the Holder Map, Solana Pay payments and Jupiter swaps on the same chain. 49 xStocks are followed (those with a DEX pool of at least $1,000 per DexScreener, server/data/solana-stocks.json). Gully Pay accepts SOL, USDC and USDT on Solana.

chunks.title: Gap alerts (Tracker)
chunks.text: Gap alerts is part of Tracker. Status: live now. Tells a signed-in user, by signed webhook or Telegram, when a stock token's gap crosses a line they set. Conditions: a gap percentage above, below or either way, or a status of premium, discount or either; the target is one stock or any stock. Alert counts by plan come from PLANS in server/plans.mjs: Free 1, Pro 10, Business 100. Webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256 in X-Gully-Signature (sha256=<hex>) with an X-Gully-Timestamp header. Alerts can also be created from the Telegram Mini App.

chunks.title: API plans (Free, Pro, Business) (Tracker)
chunks.text: API plans (Free, Pro, Business) is part of Tracker. Status: live now. Paid tiers of the tracker API that raise the per-key rate limit, add alerts and monitors, and lengthen history. Paid by crypto, with no custody. Free: $0, 600 requests a minute, 1 alert, 7 days of history, 1 contract monitor (PLANS.free). Pro: $49 per 30 days, 3,000 requests a minute, 10 alerts, 90 days of history, 10 monitors (PLANS.pro). Business: $199 per 30 days, 10,000 requests a minute, 100 alerts, 365 days of history, 50 monitors (PLANS.business). Each wallet may hold up to 5 keys on every plan; one payment buys PERIOD_DAYS (30) days. All prices and limits are read from server/plans.mjs and served at GET /api/plans.

chunks.title: Embeddable tracker widget (Widget)
chunks.text: Embeddable tracker widget is part of Widget. Status: live now. Puts live tracker data on any web page from one script tag: a ticker, a one-stock badge, a table of the widest gaps, or a Holder Map frame. Kinds via data-gully-widget: ticker, badge, table and holders. Themes: dark and light (data-theme); the script is public/widget.js, served from gullylabs.xyz/widget.js. One request per API base per minute, however many widgets are on the page. A widget builder is at /widget.

chunks.title: Holder Map (Holder Map)
chunks.text: Holder Map is part of Holder Map. Status: live now. Shows who really holds a token: the biggest wallets as bubbles, wallets that trade with each other linked as clusters, and a plain-words summary. Chains: Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain, Base, HyperEVM and Solana (HOLDER_CHAINS in server/holders.mjs); any token can be mapped, with launch checks for DeepCore launches and registered launchpads. Pools, locks, burn addresses, exchanges and the token contract are labelled grey and never counted as wallets or put in a cluster. A chain without a data source says holder data is not available; it never draws an empty or invented map. Per-tier limits come from HOLDER_MAP in server/plans.mjs: Free lists 50 holders, Pro and Business 500; the map draws at most 120. HOLDER_MAP.gated is false today, so every visitor gets the Pro features; safety warnings are never gated.

chunks.title: Launch Health score (Holder Map)
chunks.text: Launch Health score is part of Holder Map. Status: live now. Scores a DeepCore launch from 0 to 100 on liquidity, bundled buyers, the deployer's share and record, top-10 concentration and snipers. It is never behind a paywall. Weights (server/holders-intel.mjs): liquidity 20, bundle 20, deployer 20, top10 15, snipers 10, record 15. A part that cannot be read is left out and the score is computed over the rest.

chunks.title: Replay, live view and CSV (Holder Map)
chunks.text: Replay, live view and CSV is part of Holder Map. Status: live now. Replays a holder map over time with a scrubber, keeps it updating live while open, and exports the holder list as CSV. Live updates for an open map are polled from the server and shared per token for 10 seconds. CSV is GET /api/holders/:chain/:token.csv, controlled by HOLDER_MAP.tiers.*.csv. Free-tier live view lasts liveMinutes 5; Pro and Business have no limit (HOLDER_MAP in plans.mjs). A share card is served at /card.png (1200 x 630).

chunks.title: Holder Map alerts (Holder Map)
chunks.text: Holder Map alerts is part of Holder Map. Status: live now. Alerts when the largest cluster or the top-10 share of a token reaches a level or drops, by Telegram or webhook. Metric is cluster or top10; fires at an "above" percentage or after a drop of dropPts points from its high (server/alerts.mjs). Alerts count against the plan's alert limit.

chunks.title: Deep check (Holder Map)
chunks.text: Deep check is part of Holder Map. Status: live now. A paid, bounded investigation of one token that traces where top holders were funded from, shared funders, the deployer's record and snipers. Price $9 per token (HOLDER_DEEP.priceUsd); free checks a month: Free 0, Pro 3, Business 3. A 20% discount applies when bought with a paid Gully Security scan of the same contract. Budgets per check: 150 RPC calls, 12 log spans, 60 explorer calls, 120,000 ms, 12 holders traced, 3 hops. A check that hits a limit finishes "partial" with the reason. Up to 3 checks per workspace may be active and 2 run at once on the server.

chunks.title: Launchpad partner webhooks (Holder Map)
chunks.text: Launchpad partner webhooks is part of Holder Map. Status: live now. Lets a launchpad tell Gully Labs about a new token and receive a signed risk flag when the pre-built Holder Map shows warning signs. Inbound: POST /api/partners/launch with a Bearer API key; 30 launch events a minute and 1,000 a day per key; the same token is queued once per workspace per 24 hours. Outbound: launch.flagged is sent only when risk signals exist, signed with a whsec_ secret. Registered per workspace with POST /api/developer/partners/webhook.

chunks.title: Invoices and pay links (Gully Pay)
chunks.text: Invoices and pay links is part of Gully Pay. Status: live now. Non-custodial crypto billing: invoices and reusable pay links where the payer sends a plain transfer straight to the treasury (or the merchant), read back from the chain. EVM chains: Base (8453), Ethereum (1), BNB Chain (56), Arbitrum (42161), OP Mainnet (10), Polygon (137), Avalanche (43114), plus Solana; each is offered only while the Safe treasury is deployed there (server/treasury-chains.mjs). Confirmations required: Base 10, Ethereum 6, BNB Chain 15, Arbitrum 10, OP Mainnet 10, Polygon 64, Avalanche 2 (server/payments.mjs). A pay link is a fixed USD amount or an open amount between a minimum and maximum; a link makes at most LINK_INVOICES_PER_HOUR (10) invoices per IP per hour. Gully Labs never holds funds; a chainId:hash can be used once only.

chunks.title: Solana Pay (Gully Pay)
chunks.text: Solana Pay is part of Gully Pay. Status: live now. Takes SOL, USDC and USDT on Solana through Solana Pay transfer requests with a per-quote reference key. A payment counts only when the transaction is finalized. Found by reference with GET /api/solana/pay/find, or by a pasted signature.

chunks.title: Signed payment webhooks (Gully Pay)
chunks.text: Signed payment webhooks is part of Gully Pay. Status: live now. Sends signed events when an invoice is paid, expires or is cancelled. Events: invoice.paid, invoice.expired, invoice.cancelled and webhook.test. Signed with HMAC-SHA256 in X-Gully-Signature with X-Gully-Timestamp, using the endpoint's own whsec_ secret.

chunks.title: Pay with crypto button (Gully Pay)
chunks.text: Pay with crypto button is part of Gully Pay. Status: live now. An optional script that opens a Gully Pay checkout in a popup from a normal link. Add data-gully-pay="popup" to a link to a pay URL; "tab" or no script opens a new tab. The checkout cannot be put in an iframe; the script sets no cookies.

chunks.title: Live gas costs per chain (Gully Pay)
chunks.text: Live gas costs per chain is part of Gully Pay. Status: live now. Shows what a Gully Pay payment costs in gas right now on each payment chain. GET /api/pay/gas; costs assume 106k gas for a fee-proxy payment and 65k for a plain ERC-20 transfer, including the L1 data fee on OP Stack chains and Arbitrum. A chain that cannot be read says unavailable.

chunks.title: Merchant checkout (Gully Pay)
chunks.text: Merchant checkout is part of Gully Pay. Status: live now. Lets any workspace run its own non-custodial crypto checkout, paid straight into its own wallets, for a transaction fee only. Default fee is DEFAULT_FEE_BPS 50 (0.5%) of payment value above a lifetime free allowance of DEFAULT_FREE_USD ($5,000), both env-overridable (server/merchant-fees.mjs). Fee statements are issued every Monday 00:00 UTC to merchants owing at least $1; unpaid after PAUSE_AFTER_DAYS (7) the merchant's checkouts pause until paid. Merchants get pay links, invoices, signed webhooks, CSV export and a branded profile. Supports USDC, USDT and each chain's own coin on Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, OP Mainnet, Polygon and Avalanche.

chunks.title: Fee split and no-stuck-funds guards (Gully Pay)
chunks.text: Fee split and no-stuck-funds guards is part of Gully Pay. Status: live now. Collects the merchant fee inside the payment through Request Network's ERC20FeeProxy on stablecoins, with guards so funds can never end up stuck in the proxy. A plain transfer, QR code or link never names a fee proxy as recipient on any chain (server/fee-proxy-guard.mjs). Split calls use only USDC or USDT, with the fee strictly between 0 and the amount. An hourly monitor reads every known proxy's balance and raises an admin alert on a non-zero balance (server/fee-proxy-monitor.mjs).

chunks.title: One-click Safe deployment (Gully Pay)
chunks.text: One-click Safe deployment is part of Gully Pay. Status: live now. Deploys a Safe multisig at the same address on another chain from inside the app, with the user's own wallet signing. The server works out the factory call and never holds a key or sends a transaction. Uses Safe's CREATE2 proxy factory so the address matches across chains.

chunks.title: AI Security Scan (Gully Security)
chunks.text: AI Security Scan is part of Gully Security. Status: live now. A self-serve automated scan of a deployed contract, a Solidity repository, an upload or a web2 codebase. It is an AI review only until the static-tools worker runs, and is never called an audit. Inputs: deployed address, GitHub repo and commit, uploaded file, or web2 repo (checklist mode). Chains: Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, OP Mainnet, BNB Chain, Polygon, Avalanche, Sepolia and Base Sepolia (server/security/chains.mjs). Price $99 per scan beyond the monthly allowance (SECURITY.scan.priceUsd); free scans a month: Free 1, Pro 3, Business 10; up to 2 active scans; uploads up to 2,000,000 bytes (server/plans.mjs). Every report is labelled "AI review only — static tools unavailable" and every finding has verifiedByHuman false.

chunks.title: Published scan reports (Gully Security)
chunks.text: Published scan reports is part of Gully Security. Status: live now. Scan reports can be published and read as web pages, with findings, locations and draft proofs of concept. Pages at /security/reports and /security/reports/:id; API under /api/security/reports. Reports state the target, tools run or not run, the commit or address and a point-in-time disclaimer.

chunks.title: Contract monitors (Gully Security)
chunks.text: Contract monitors is part of Gully Security. Status: live now. Watches a contract and tells you by Telegram or signed webhook when a privileged change happens. Watches ownership transfers, ERC-1967 admin and upgrade changes, role grants and revokes, pauses, large outflows, and Safe owner or threshold changes. One pass per chain every LOOP_MS (60,000 ms); each event is delivered at most once. Monitors per plan come from PLANS: Free 1, Pro 10, Business 50.

chunks.title: Security Review (Gully Security)
chunks.text: Security Review is part of Gully Security. Status: live now. People on the team read the code in scope and write up what they find. Quoted per project after a request. SECURITY.review is quoted with no list price and available (server/plans.mjs). Requested through the form at /security (POST /api/security/review-requests).

chunks.title: Roadmap: Audit (Gully Security), not available yet
chunks.text: Audit (Gully Security) is planned and is NOT available yet: coming soon, with no date. Do not tell anyone they can use it today. A premium audit tier is not offered yet. Gully Labs has published no audit reports. SECURITY.audit has available: false (server/plans.mjs). The roadmap says audits open only once the people, process and public record exist.

chunks.title: Gully Score (Gully Score)
chunks.text: Gully Score is part of Gully Score. Status: live now. A 0 to 100 reading of how a contract is controlled and how it has behaved, from public evidence only, with every component, weight and source shown. Nine components with weights: code verified 15, who controls it 20, delay on changes 10, can the code change 10, recent privileged changes 10, liquidity locked 10, holder spread 10, Gully Security review 10, age 5 (COMPONENTS in server/gully-score.mjs). A component that cannot be read is left out, never scored as zero; below MIN_COVERAGE (40) of the 100 weight points no score is given. Paying Gully Labs never changes a score. Methodology at GET /api/score/methodology.

chunks.title: Score badge (Gully Score)
chunks.text: Score badge is part of Gully Score. Status: live now. An SVG badge of a contract's score that a project can embed on its own site. Rendered by server/gully-score.mjs as an SVG labelled GULLY SCORE.

chunks.title: Gully AI assistant (Gully AI)
chunks.text: Gully AI assistant is part of Gully AI. Status: live now. Answers questions about Gully Labs from its own docs and live data, cites its sources and says it does not know when it does not. Retrieval is hybrid: BM25, a synonym-expanded BM25 and, when VOYAGE_API_KEY is set, embeddings, fused by reciprocal-rank fusion. Live tools include get_plans, get_stock, get_top_gaps, deepcore_launches, deepcore_pool, get_holders, get_gully_score, get_published_reports, get_pay_chains, get_status and get_pay_gas; signed-in users also get get_my_store, get_my_usage and get_my_alerts. Default answer model is claude-haiku-5-5 (ASK_MODEL); the log keeps a salted IP hash only, for 90 days. Per-visitor limits default to 6 a minute and 60 a day; ASK_DAILY_LIMIT caps all surfaces at 2000 a day. It runs on the site (/ask), the docs, the app, ⌘K and Telegram (/ask).

chunks.title: @GullyLabsBot commands and alerts (Telegram bot)
chunks.text: @GullyLabsBot commands and alerts is part of Telegram bot. Status: live now. A Telegram bot with a menu for gaps, movers, new DeepCore launches, Holder Map, contract scans, Gully Score and Gully AI, plus alert delivery. Private-chat commands: start, app, gap, top, movers, launches, holders, alerts, security, score, ask, help, stop. Groups get gap, top, launches and help. Alerts can be paused, muted for 24 hours, tested or deleted from the chat. A chat is connected to a wallet account from the app dashboard.

chunks.title: News channel gate (Telegram bot)
chunks.text: News channel gate is part of Telegram bot. Status: live now. Asks users to follow @GullyLabsNews to use the bot's features, while leaving alerts, mute, pause, delete and unlink open. If membership cannot be checked, the gate lets people through. The same gate applies in the Mini App.

chunks.title: Telegram Mini App (Mini App)
chunks.text: Telegram Mini App is part of Mini App. Status: live now. The Gully app inside Telegram, with stock gaps, DeepCore launches and alerts for the account linked to your chat. Served at gullylabs.xyz/tg; each request carries Telegram initData, validated with HMAC-SHA256 and refused after 24 hours. Routes: /api/tg/me, /sparks, /launches, /alerts and /announcements.

chunks.title: New DeepCore launch alerts (Telegram bot)
chunks.text: New DeepCore launch alerts is part of Telegram bot. Status: live now. Alerts when a new token launches on DeepCore, on any chain or one you pick. DeepCore chains: BNB Chain (56), HyperEVM (999), Robinhood Chain (4663) and Base (8453).

chunks.title: Gully Analytics (Gully Analytics)
chunks.text: Gully Analytics is part of Gully Analytics. Status: live now. Privacy-friendly web analytics with Web3 events, a fork of Umami, that a wallet signs up for in the app and pays for with Gully Pay. Free trial of ANALYTICS_TRIAL_DAYS (14) days with 1 site and 10,000 events a month. Starter: $19, 3 sites, 100,000 events a month. Growth: $79, 10 sites, 1,000,000 events a month (ANALYTICS_PLANS; the prices are placeholders until the owner sets them). After a lapse, events are refused but the dashboard stays readable for ANALYTICS_GRACE_DAYS (30) days. Events over quota are answered 402 by the proxy at analytics.gullylabs.xyz.

chunks.title: Gully Labs App dashboard (App)
chunks.text: Gully Labs App dashboard is part of App. Status: live now. A wallet-signed-in dashboard at app.gullylabs.xyz for keys, alerts, usage, billing, analytics, security, Gully Pay and the other services. Sign-in is Sign-In with Ethereum (EIP-4361), including smart-contract wallets via EIP-1271 and ERC-6492. The old developers host was retired on 2026-10-17; /app and /developers on the main site redirect to the app.

chunks.title: Teams and workspaces (App)
chunks.text: Teams and workspaces is part of App. Status: live now. Every wallet is a workspace; owners invite teammates by wallet or link with roles, and an activity log records changes. Roles: owner, admin, developer, billing, viewer (server/workspaces.mjs). CSV exports of usage and payments: GET /api/developer/export/usage.csv and payments.csv. Usage notices fire at 80% and 100% of a key's per-minute limit.

chunks.title: Public status page (Docs)
chunks.text: Public status page is part of Docs. Status: live now. A public page and JSON endpoint showing the health of the API, tracker data, DeepCore poller, Telegram bot, payment RPCs, Gully AI, the scan engine, monitors and Holder Map sources. Checks run every 60 seconds with 24 hours of samples kept; incidents open and close on state changes. Endpoint: GET /api/status.

chunks.title: Docs site and changelog (Docs)
chunks.text: Docs site and changelog is part of Docs. Status: live now. Documentation for every product at docs.gullylabs.xyz, with a searchable sidebar, an API reference, a roadmap and a dated changelog. Pages cover the tracker, API, widget, SDK, Holder Map, Gully Pay, Gully Security, Gully Score, Gully AI, Telegram, Solana, Chain Kit, status, roadmap and changelog (src/docs/nav.ts).

chunks.title: Cross-venue live stats (Gully Labs)
chunks.text: Cross-venue live stats is part of Gully Labs. Status: live now. The home page shows live figures read from each Gully Labs project's own public API, each with its source. Venues read: Cartel Family, DeepCore, PeddleSwap, Peddles and PeddleQuest (server/stats.mjs). A venue that cannot be read is reported as an error, never as zeros; a token-denominated figure is never added to a dollar total.

chunks.title: Engineering services (Gully Labs)
chunks.text: Engineering services is part of Gully Labs. Status: live now. Gully Labs takes on smart contract, dApp, chain infrastructure and security work on request. Smart Contracts (6-12 weeks), dApps and Frontends (8-16 weeks), Chain Infrastructure (8-20 weeks) and Gully Security (quoted) are listed in src/content/services.ts. Enquiries go through POST /api/contact.

chunks.title: Blog (Gully Labs)
chunks.text: Blog is part of Gully Labs. Status: live now. A self-hosted Ghost blog at blog.gullylabs.xyz with generated share images. Share images are 1200 x 630 PNGs rendered at /og/blog/<slug>.png. New posts can auto-post to the @GullyLabsNews channel.

chunks.title: Token logo service (Gully Labs)
chunks.text: Token logo service is part of Gully Labs. Status: live now. Serves token logos by chain and address for the whole stack, from the first source that returns a valid image. GET /api/logo/:chain/:address at 64, 128 or 256 px. Sources in order: DeepCore, DexScreener, Jupiter or the xStocks logo, CoinGecko, Trust Wallet.

chunks.title: Chain Kit managed explorer (Chain Kit)
chunks.text: Chain Kit managed explorer is part of Chain Kit. Status: live now. A branded Blockscout block explorer for your EVM chain, deployed and run by Gully Labs. Available on request. Requested from the app (POST /api/developer/chain-kit/request) or the contact form. Blockscout and our deployment layer are GPL-3.0. Rollup profiles cover Arbitrum Nitro and Orbit chains.

chunks.title: Gully Chains waitlist (Gully Chains)
chunks.text: Gully Chains waitlist is part of Gully Chains. Status: live now. A waitlist in the app for Gully Chains devnet news. No chain is running yet. POST /api/developer/chains-waitlist saves an email against the wallet. POST /api/chains/waitlist is the public form on /chains; the app waitlist remains.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3 (Arbitrum chain) (Gully Chains), not available yet
chunks.text: Gully L3 (Arbitrum chain) (Gully Chains) is planned and is NOT available yet: coming soon, with no date. Do not tell anyone they can use it today. A planned Arbitrum chain settling to Arbitrum One with Chain Kit as explorer, Gully Pay native and Hyperlane interop. Spec written, nothing running. Stages: S0 light devnet (Nitro dev mode, chain id 412346, prepared but not started), S1 public devnet on Arbitrum Sepolia, S2 production L3. chunks.title: Map any token (Holder Map)
chunks.text: Map any token is part of Holder Map. Status: live now. The Holder Map accepts any ERC-20 on four EVM chains and any SPL token on Solana, not only DeepCore launches and stock tokens. A pasted address is checked to be a token first. Chains in HOLDER_CHAINS (server/holders.mjs): Robinhood Chain (4663), BNB Chain (56), Base (8453), HyperEVM (999) and Solana. An address is probed before anything is built: an ERC-20 must answer decimals() and totalSupply(); on Solana it must be a mint. With no chain given, every supported chain is checked at once. Limits for non-listed tokens (ANY in server/holders-any.mjs): 5 new maps per IP per minute, 30 a minute across all IPs, 2 built at once; address probes 8 per IP per minute and 60 a minute overall. Maps already built are free. Launch checks and the Launch Health score stay limited to DeepCore launches and launchpads in the registry; a plain token gets holders, clusters and concentration. GET /api/holders/sources reports per chain whether tokens map with full history, as top holders only, or not yet.

chunks.title: Launchpad registry (Peddles, PeddleSwap) (Holder Map)
chunks.text: Launchpad registry (Peddles, PeddleSwap) is part of Holder Map. Status: live now. A registry of launchpads lets the Holder Map recognise a token as a launch from a known launchpad. Peddles and PeddleSwap are the first two entries. Peddles: Robinhood Chain 4663, Base 8453 and BNB Chain 56, looked up through its API with the PoolRegistered fee-hook event as a fallback. PeddleSwap: Robinhood Chain 4663 and Base 8453, looked up through its launches API. Lookups time out at 6 s (HTTP_MS), run at most 4 at a time (MAX_INFLIGHT) and 120 uncached lookups a minute (MAX_PER_MIN). Positive results are cached for 24 hours and "not a launch" for 10 minutes. An unknown or unreachable launchpad degrades to a generic token map.

chunks.section: Peddles and PeddleQuest read on chain (building)
chunks.text: Peddles and PeddleQuest read on chain (Ecosystem) is being built and is NOT available yet: coming soon, with no date. Do not tell anyone they can use it today. Peddles and PeddleQuest figures would be read straight from their contracts instead of only from the venues' APIs, with a live ledger series and an on-chain panel on their project pages. Chains read: Base 8453, Robinhood Chain 4663, Arc 5042 and BNB Chain 56. Reads PoolRegistered, FeeAccrued, SniperFeeAccrued, CreatorSwept, HoldersSwept, LaunchFeePaid, FeeCollected, CollectionCreated, BuybackAndBurn (Base), PeddleQuest escrow, promotion market and badge events, and Uniswap v4 PoolManager Swap, ModifyLiquidity and Initialize events. PeddleQuest contracts are at the same addresses on all four chains: escrow 0x1626…CadE, market 0x704E…4849, badge 0x6DA2…AE91. Backfills once from the fee hook's deploy block, then updates every 30 seconds (PEDDLES_LOOP=off disables it). Contracts are re-checked for code at runtime. Endpoint GET /api/peddles/onchain (cache 20 s); also available as a Vercel function. DefiLlama stays as a cross-check; if our all-time differs by more than 10% ours is shown with a footnote. An asset with no price feed is counted as unpriced, never as $0. The home hero ledger gains a pulsing live dot and a LIVE swap counter; project pages for peddles and peddlequest gain an on-chain panel listing each contract with a link to the explorer.

chunks.title: Launchpad (DeepCore)
chunks.text: Launchpad is part of DeepCore. Status: live now. A token, its pool and locked liquidity are created in one transaction, with a decaying anti-snipe fee at the open. LaunchpadKitV2 opens a launch on a concentrated-liquidity range or a shaped Bin distribution Liquidity is locked forever via DeepCoreLPLocker / DeepCoreBinLPLocker Anti-snipe fee: LaunchGuardHook caps the initial fee at 50% (MAX_INITIAL_FEE) and the final fee at 10%; README states 50% at the open, 10% on Bin, decaying over at least 60 seconds Optional creator tax is capped at 10% (MAX_TAX_BPS = 1000) and expires by itself, at most 180 days LaunchpadKitV2 is recorded in the SDK address book on Base, BNB Chain, HyperEVM and Robinhood Chain at the same address 0x78781DC6... Wizard is market-cap-first with a $3.5K-equivalent default per the README

chunks.text: Hosted Launchpads and DEXes is part of DeepCore. Status: live now. Anyone can open their own Launchpad or DEX on the core in one transaction, with a share of fees going to the site. DeepCorePadFactory clones a pad at the same address on every chain (0x7878647B... in the address book) Owner, name, brand and terms are stored on chain Hosted site can use a deepcore.fun subdomain or the owner's own domain, with a theme pack and its own fee share (README) Contracts: DeepCorePad, DeepCorePadFactory in packages/launchpad/src/pad

chunks.title: Best-price router (DeepCore)
chunks.text: Best-price router is part of DeepCore. Status: live now. Swaps route across DeepCore pools and other venues. DeepCore pools carry no router fee; fills on other venues pay a small capped fee. DeepCoreFillRouter charges feeBps() on fills elsewhere; README states 0.15% The fee is bounded in the contract by ABSOLUTE_MAX_FEE_BPS = 100 (1%) Fee changes use a notice period of up to MAX_FEE_NOTICE_SECONDS = 30 days fillRouter is 0x78786244... on all four chains in the SDK address book

chunks.title: Swap (PeddleSwap)
chunks.text: Swap is part of PeddleSwap. Status: live now. V2 and V3 liquidity behind one router, with an Auto mode that picks the better venue. Auto mode races V2 against all four V3 fee tiers (0.01%, 0.05%, 0.30%, 1.00%) Exact-input and exact-output swaps, multi-hop paths, native ETH on both sides, Permit2 TokenValidator flash-borrows a pasted token to detect fee-on-transfer and honeypot behaviour, and separates 'tested clean' from 'could not be tested' Contracts deployed per deployments files on Robinhood Chain (4663), Arc (5042) and Base (8453), plus Sepolia The README still says 'live on Sepolia'; the repo's mainnet deployment files and projects.ts list Robinhood, Base and Arc

chunks.title: Token and LP locker (PeddleSwap)
chunks.text: Token and LP locker is part of PeddleSwap. Status: live now. Locks tokens, V2 LP and V3 positions with no admin unlock. Locked V3 positions keep earning fees. PeddleLockerERC20 for fungible tokens and V2 LP; PeddleLockerERC721 for V3/V4 positions and NFTs No admin unlock, no emergency withdraw, no upgrade path; unlock times can only be extended Locks are transferable and splittable; a split inherits the parent's unlock time Locker addresses recorded for 4663, 5042 and 8453

chunks.title: Token launcher and creator fees (PeddleSwap)
chunks.text: Token launcher and creator fees is part of PeddleSwap. Status: live now. An ownerless token factory with a fixed-supply token, and a fee router that pays a share of swaps back to the token's project. PeddleToken has no mint, owner, pause, blocklist or proxy (ADR 0006) PeddleTokenFactory deploys with CREATE2 under a caller-derived salt tokenFactory has a non-zero address on Robinhood Chain (4663) and Sepolia; it is the zero address in the Base (8453) and Arc (5042) files PeddleFeeRouter pays a creator share; registering one is an owner-only call

chunks.title: Stock-paired token launches (Peddles)
chunks.text: Stock-paired token launches is part of Peddles. Status: live now. Launch a token whose pool is quoted in a tokenised stock. All supply goes to liquidity locked from block zero. Built on Uniswap v4 single-sided liquidity; the liquidity position is permanently locked and there is no bonding curve or migration Deployed default allocation is 100% liquidity; setAllocation refuses a non-zero burn leg Live on Base 8453, Robinhood Chain 4663, BNB Smart Chain 56 and Arc 5042 since 2026-10-01 per CLAUDE.md Launch fee is about $2 on every launch type, paid in the chain's native currency Starting market cap is about $3.5K on every launch type and chain Anti-sniper opening-tax window defaults to 3 minutes of wall-clock time on every chain; Arc stock pairs stay hidden until issuer tokens are verified

chunks.title: Holder rewards (Peddles)
chunks.text: Holder rewards is part of Peddles. Status: live now. A distributor pays launched-token holders from the token's fee stream, notified on every transfer. PeddlesHolderRewards and PeddlesHolderRewardsFactory in contracts/src Launched tokens hold a write-once holderRewards address and send a notification after every transfer, mint and burn, with a fixed gas stipend The notification moves no value PeddlesNftHolderRewards does the same for NFT collection holders

chunks.title: Other launch types (Peddles)
chunks.text: Other launch types is part of Peddles. Status: live now. Beyond stock pairs: WETH-paired, Clog, handle and NFT launches. Clog: PeddlesClogVault sells a marketing allocation into the pool in capped slices and the creator pulls the proceeds Handle launches: PeddlesHandleLauncher launches a coin whose creator fees go to an X account's pot; deployment files exist for 8453, 4663, 5042, 56 NFT launchpad: bonding-curve collections that graduate into tokens (PeddlesNFTFactory, graduation orchestrators) Solana launchpad and deploy-from-a-tweet are marked coming soon in CLAUDE.md

chunks.title: Perps (Peddles)
chunks.text: Perps is part of Peddles. Status: live now. Perpetual markets via a factory and hook, live on all four mainnets. Deployment files 4663-perp.json, 8453-perp.json, 56-perp.json and 5042-perp.json each have status 'live' Robinhood perp deployment dated 2026-09-30 Contracts: PeddlesPerpFactory, PeddlesPerpHookDeployer, PeddlesPerpTreasury, PeddlesPerpHook

chunks.title: Terminal and Telegram trade bot (Peddles)
chunks.text: Terminal and Telegram trade bot is part of Peddles. Status: live now. A multi-chain token terminal at peddles.xyz/terminal and a Telegram trade bot that uses the same API. Terminal API chain slugs: ethereum, bsc, base, robinhood, arc, solana Terminal is served at peddles.xyz/terminal (CLAUDE.md domain table) Trade bot wallets are custodial: keys are created and held by the bot, encrypted with AES-256-GCM Prediction games are non-wagering; bots default to paper trading

chunks.title: Arcade (Peddles)
chunks.text: Arcade is part of Peddles. Status: in beta (usable, and still changing). A launchpad for browser games, with server-validated XP and leaderboards. Holders of a coin get ranked play on its game. Repo status says 'phase 2': creator platform with a 9-step game wizard, uploads and a build pipeline Game templates in the repo: endless-runner, racing, party-arena, arena-shooter, retro-fps, candle-runner, puzzle A coin's game is materialised on first open; a run is 'ranked' only if a verified wallet holds the coin Non-wagering: XP, points, badges and leaderboards only CLAUDE.md of peddles-launchpad places the Arcade app at peddles.xyz/arcade peddles-arcade-shooters is a near-copy of the same repo without the party-arena template

chunks.title: Quest reward escrow (PeddleQuest)
chunks.text: Quest reward escrow is part of PeddleQuest. Status: live now. Quest reward pools are escrowed on chain first and paid out by Merkle proof. PeddlesQuestEscrow holds reward pools; creator deposits gross and the fee is taken once at deposit, never from participants Participants claim by Merkle proof; the operator publishes the root Same contract addresses on Base 8453, Robinhood Chain 4663, BSC 56 and Arc 5042 per docs/monetization.md (escrow 0x16267bE6...) Contracts are described as unaudited; the repo says never to claim an audit Starting fee model: quest creation free, deposit fee 3% (permanent cap 10%), per-quest pool cap $100,000

chunks.title: Soulbound badges (PeddleQuest)
chunks.text: Soulbound badges is part of PeddleQuest. Status: live now. An optional non-transferable proof-of-completion badge minted after a quest. PeddlesQuestBadge is soulbound; transfers revert with a Soulbound error Badge mint fee starts at $0.30 with a $10 permanent cap PeddlesQuestBadge address 0x6DA219d4... is the same on all four chains per docs/monetization.md

chunks.title: Promotion slots (PeddleQuest)
chunks.text: Promotion slots is part of PeddleQuest. Status: live now. Trending and banner placement is sold on chain, so what was bought is publicly recorded. PeddlesPromotionMarket sells time-boxed trending slots and banners for native currency, flat rate per day Starting rate is $3 per day with a $500 per day cap Proceeds go to the treasury

chunks.title: Task verification and eligibility rules (PeddleQuest)
chunks.text: Task verification and eligibility rules is part of PeddleQuest. Status: live now. Off-chain checks for X, Discord and wallet tasks, with eligibility and sybil rules set in the quest wizard. Docs cover X verification, Discord verification and general verification Quest wizard has an Eligibility step (src/modules/quest/pq-wizard/steps/EligibilityStep.tsx) that references sybil rules Frontend routes include quest, leaderboard, loyalty, referral-invite and profile Production builds carry the four mainnets only (testnets disabled)

chunks.title: Social feed and copy trading (Cartel Family)
chunks.text: Social feed and copy trading is part of Cartel Family. Status: live now. A wallet-native social trading app with a public feed, follows and copy-trade tracking. Public feed with posts, trades and token calls; follows, reactions, replies and direct messages (README) Copy-trade tracking and trader profiles with win rate and PnL (README) Domain cartel.family is defined in site_config.py per CLAUDE.md Python/Flask backend with SQLite, deployed from a Dockerfile (README says Railway)

chunks.title: Multi-chain automated trading bot (Cartel Family)
chunks.text: Multi-chain automated trading bot is part of Cartel Family. Status: live now. An AI-scored bot trades on a user's behalf with configurable limits. Chains: Solana plus five EVM chains (BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon, Robinhood Chain) Solana swaps use Jupiter; EVM swaps use the 0x API Bot scores tokens every 30 seconds; user sets take-profit, stop-loss, trade size and a daily loss limit Performance fee on profitable trades only (README); CLAUDE.md records a 0.80% per-leg revenue rate set on 2026-10-10 Private keys are encrypted (Fernet with a wallet-derived HMAC)

chunks.title: Live market and one-send wallet (Cartel Family)
chunks.text: Live market and one-send wallet is part of Cartel Family. Status: live now. Live market discovery with a launches tab, plus a single send path across all chains. Live Market page with Trending, New Pairs and Gainers; a Launches tab (New / Hot / Near graduation) is described in CLAUDE.md wallet_send.send_funds is the only way money leaves a wallet: native coin or USDC on Solana and all five EVM chains, behind POST /api/send One EVM address works across the five EVM chains Gas sponsorship for empty EVM wallets is optional via GAS_SPONSOR_PRIVATE_KEY
